items.title: Webhooks that wake room agents (Space-bound inbound endpoints)
items.summary: Let a Space manager create a secret webhook endpoint bound to a room and an agent. Ingestion Plane verifies the provider or HMAC signature, dedups the delivery, filters by JSON path and caps the payload; Model Plane capability-core then receives a wake envelope on the same trigger path schedules use, with the payload wrapped as untrusted data, and Control Plane decides every fire under the endpoint owner's authority.
items.whyItMatters: It turns room agents from chat-only into event-driven coworkers: a GitHub PR, a Stripe dispute or a monitoring alert starts work in the room. The agent-centric references that have it (qm, buzz) treat it as the way agents are triggered by the outside world, and it reuses the schedule fire path Verevon already governs. The same unattended-turn plumbing also unblocks per-agent email (F-t1-075 (R-t1-06-10)).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; differentiator (webhook triggers also appear in Slack/Teams workflow builders)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm's WebhookReceiver.deliver(id, headers, rawBody) runs a per-provider verifier (github, slack, stripe, linear, generic HMAC) with constant-time compare, handles provider handshakes, derives a delivery id for dedup, filters events by JSON path (e.g. action in [opened]), caps the payload at 16,000 chars in a wake envelope, wraps it as untrusted content and dispatches it like a cron fire under the endpoint owner's authority. The secret is shown once; each endpoint has an event log. Buzz adds outbound calls with SSRF protection.

verevonToday.gap: The baseline recorded 'absent' after searching only the Spaces router and Convex schema; this pass found more (SRC). integration-corev2 already receives org-level provider webhooks at /api/v1/webhooks/:provider (signature check, normalise, tenant resolution, stored with a duplicate flag, published as verevon.ingestion.integration.webhook_received on NATS), and the only consumer found is conversation-core's inbox. Missing for Spaces: per-room secret endpoints (the route only accepts providers in the fixed catalogue), generic HMAC and GitHub/Stripe/Linear-style verifiers with path filters and a payload cap, a consumer that turns the event into a Control-decided capability-core fire bound to space_ref, and any UI. bridge-core's outbound webhook adapter (durable, retrying) is not wired to Spaces.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane integration-corev2: add a space-webhook route family (endpoint id in the path) backed by an endpoint record owned by Control (secret shown once, space_ref, agent binding, filter, size cap, owner), reuse the existing verify, normalise, dedup and store path, and publish a wake event carrying only a reference (as webhook_received does, with the stored payload fetched by id). Model Plane capability-core: consume the event as a trigger variant beside schedules, obtain a Control fire decision per delivery (owner authority, privacy/ZDR claims), then start an unattended turn through the Space scheduled-run machinery with the payload wrapped as untrusted content. Frontend: endpoint management and a delivery log in the Agent or Work tab; results post into the room. ZDR rooms keep payloads out of retention. Outbound calls (agent or workflow calling external URLs) can reuse bridge-core's webhook adapter once its SSRF/egress controls are confirmed (INF).
dependencies: Control endpoint record and per-delivery fire-decision contract
Unattended no-live-user turn for Space scheduled runs (capability-core PrepareScheduledRunThread)
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (receive and verify); Model Plane capability-core (trigger); Control Plane (endpoint record, fire decision)
items.risks: Prompt injection through payloads (bound and wrap as untrusted); webhook secret leakage; flood and cost control; ZDR rooms must not retain payloads; at-least-once delivery means replays need idempotent fire keys.

verevon.exactGap: integration-corev2 already receives org-level provider webhooks at POST /api/v1/webhooks/:provider (fixed provider catalogue, github/shopify/slack/stripe/meta signature verifiers, tenant resolution, dedup by stored event id, NATS publish carrying only a stored-payload reference fetched by GET /internal/webhooks/events/:id), but nothing is Space-bound: no per-room secret endpoint, no generic HMAC or JSON-path filter, no payload cap, and conversation-core's inbox is the only subscriber. The wake machinery it would reuse is not ready: Control's schedule-create, schedule-fire and watch-create decisions require a personal Space and refuse ZDR for schedules, the scheduled runtime is a single no-tool 1024-token inference call, and the S4.3 watch primitive stops at 'recorded' with delivery unbuilt (the gateway reports watches_not_built).

Payloads are attacker-controlled: carry them as unscreened content, never with tool access in the same turn. ZDR rooms must drop payloads. Delivery of the result (S4.4) is unbuilt.

Do not state that Control decides every fire as if it already works for rooms.

verevon.verdictReason: The org-level receive/verify/dedup half exists and the plan overlaps S4.3, but the claimed wake path rests on Control and runtime pieces that exist only for personal Spaces and tool-free runs.

items.title: Room visibility, directory and self-join (org-public or private), with a late-joiner history rule
items.summary: Add open/private visibility to named rooms in Control, a paged directory of org-public rooms the caller is not in (member count, description), and a self-join decision that grants exactly room membership with the default role; private rooms return not-found to non-members. Record join and leave sequence per membership so thread reads can be limited to a tenure window, and make membership-change and revocation delivery durable. Self-join must never widen the ACL on documents bound to the room.
items.whyItMatters: Browse and join is table stakes in buzz, Slack and Teams; today a person sees only rooms they were added to. Control already stores a privacy_revision to build on.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz; slack
others: qm (tri-state membership, deny-on-unknown fallback; sequence-bounded participant windows)
slack (public and private channels, no record in this category)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-02-02] 3 of 5 for discovery and self-join (buzz, teams, qm); tenure windows 1 of 5 (qm); table-stakes for discovery, unique for tenure [R-t1-04-05] 3 of 5 sources; table-stakes (Slack evidence is DOC only; buzz open channel directory is SRC)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-02-02] room.visibility in {open, private}. GET /rooms/directory returns open rooms in the org the caller is not in, paged and separate from the member poll. POST /rooms/{id}/join self-grants the default role only for open rooms; private rooms 404 to non-members; when membership is unknown, deny. QM adds ParticipantWindow{validFromSeq, validToSeq} on membership rows that filters transcript reads and approvals, and a roster-version fence on enqueue. [R-t1-04-05] Rooms carry visibility (public or private); the directory lists public rooms in the org with member count and description; join is a self-add membership allowed only for public rooms; an external directory lists cross-org connections with status (pending, active).

Fencing by authority and audience revision is strong, but late-joiner history and durable delivery of revocations are not covered. [R-t1-04-05] Space listing is filtered to the caller's Control index (spaces.rs:2747-2810). A grep in this step found only an is_organization_room flag (the org's own room, pinned in the sidebar) and no visibility field under Control Plane user-core/internal/spaces, so there is no public visibility, browse route or self-join route.

items.approach: [R-t1-02-02] Control Plane (user-core): add visibility to registered_spaces (bump privacy_revision on change) and a self-join decision that writes a membership only for open rooms and org members, keeping thread_read_entitled and the owner-plane knowledge ACL in force. Store join and leave sequence per membership and carry the reader's window in the thread-read decision (shared_thread_read_decision.go) so Session Core filters transcripts; make the history rule a room setting (full history default for open rooms, strict window default for guests). Application Plane: mirror visibility on spaces and add a directory query separate from the member list. Gateway: GET /api/v1/spaces/directory, POST /api/v1/spaces/{space_ref}/join. Frontend: browse dialog in CoreSidebarSpacesPanel. Move membership_changed to JetStream or an outbox. [R-t1-04-05] Control Plane (user-core spaces): add visibility to the Space record and a self-join decision that adds the caller as a member of an org-public Space and nothing else; bound documents keep their own owner-plane ACL checks. Gateway: GET browse route returning only org-public Spaces of the caller's active org. Frontend: directory page with search by name and a Join button. Membership changes must propagate to Session Core reliably.
dependencies: Room role management (F-t1-022 (R-t1-02-01)) for the default join role
Model Plane Session Core thread-read filtering by window
Reliable membership-change propagation to Session Core (today plain, lossy NATS)
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (visibility, join decision, tenure) with Model Plane (tenure-window read filter) and Frontend Plane (directory page)
items.risks: [R-t1-02-02] A self-joiner could read history from before they joined; decide the tenure rule first (Slack shows full history, QM windows strictly). Open-room names in the directory must respect residency and ZDR. Self-join must never widen an owner-plane ACL, so the knowledge intersection still applies after join. [R-t1-04-05] A public room with bound documents may look like it grants document access; the UI must show that documents stay owner-ACL gated. Joining a room must never widen an owner-plane ACL.

verevon.exactGap: No visibility, directory, self-join or tenure rule exists (SRC): registered_spaces has no visibility column (privacy_revision is only a revision counter), space_memberships has no valid_from or join sequence, the gateway route table has no browse or join route, and the sidebar and listing show only Spaces in the caller Control index (a non-member already gets 404, so private-by-membership is today the only mode). Session Core applies only a recipient-audience-revision ceiling to shared-thread reads (rows newer than the reader decision are dropped), never a floor, so any current member reads the full history. membership_changed is published by user-core through JetStream fire-and-forget (errors only logged, no outbox) and consumed by session-core with a plain NATS subscribe by design, so a missed event is never replayed; the item text says "plain NATS" for the publisher, which is slightly off.
reuse: Control registered_spaces and space_authority_revisions (bump privacy_revision and membership_revision on visibility or join)
gateway control_space_index plus Application labels composition in list_personal_spaces (the directory can use the same intersect pattern)
Application spaces table for name and topic; SpacesIndexPage and CoreSidebarSpacesPanel for the UI
session-core audience-ceiling filter on messages and threads (basis for a floor, see approach)
Control ReplaceMemberships and the Application intent record for the membership write
verevon.constraints: ADR-0001 (SRC): Application owns Space name, kind and lifecycle; Control owns membership, privacy decisions and revisions, so visibility belongs in Control and name or description in Application, and the directory must compose both in the gateway as the index already does. Membership writes today are an Application declarative full replace into Control (ReplaceMemberships deactivates managed users not declared, spaceMembers.ts:243), so a Control-native self-join would be revoked at the next sync of that room unless the self-join goes through the Application intent record or the sync is scoped by source (INF from SRC). Product intent is that team and external Spaces are visible only to explicit participants (SRC UI research doc), so org-public rooms are a deliberate Slack-style policy change: private by default and opt-in per org. Never widen an owner-plane ACL on join (ADR-0001). Room names in the directory must respect residency and ZDR. The tenure window needs a join marker: the existing per-message recipient_audience_revision stamp is a candidate floor (INF, low confidence, not traced through Application audience registration).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: membership_changed already goes out over JetStream; the non-durable part is the plain-subscribe consumer in session-core (by design) and the absence of a publisher outbox. For self-join, pick the membership writer first (Application intent record versus Control source-tagged writes) and keep rooms private by default with org-public opt-in. Default the history rule to full history for open rooms, which is today behaviour and costs nothing, and defer the strict tenure floor to the guest work (F-t1-053). Split the item: visibility, directory and join is M; tenure window and durable delivery are the L part.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged at L, but recommend splitting; the visibility, directory and join slice alone is M once the membership writer is decided.
verevon.verdictReason: Absence confirmed and the feature is table stakes, but the approach must resolve who writes room membership (declarative Application sync would clobber a Control self-join) and fix the NATS description.

items.title: Searchable people-and-agent directory with an agent-readable resolver
items.summary: Add a Control Plane directory search (org members and registered agents by name or email prefix) that returns only subjects the caller may see, expose it through the gateway to the add-member and DM pickers, and give agents a resolve tool that answers ok, ambiguous (with candidates) or none (with a reason).
items.whyItMatters: Needed to add members, start DMs and group rooms (Teams-like team support) and for agents to address the right human. All five references have it; Verevon has per-Space rosters and an org member list but nothing searchable across the org.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 5 of 5 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: One picker resolves org directory, saved contacts and external users (external found only by exact email/SIP to prevent enumeration), with guest/external tags and chat/call/block actions; results ranked by recent interaction. qm adds resolver vocabulary for agents: ok, ambiguous, none, not-in-channel, unlinked login.

verevonToday.gap: A per-Space roster (person or agent kind, role) and an org member list exist. There is no searchable directory across the org or Spaces (a grep for directory or member-search routes in gateway orgs/ found none), no external or guest lookup, no contact actions, and no resolver with agent-readable errors.

items.approach: Control Plane (identity owner): GET /orgs/{id}/directory/search (name/email prefix, people and agents) returning only subjects visible to the caller; external lookup by exact email once external access exists. Gateway exposes it to pickers and to an agent resolve tool returning ok|ambiguous|none. Frontend: shared picker component used by add-member, DM start and the @ menu.
dependencies: DMs, group rooms and guest model (other audit categories)
items.planeOwner: Control Plane
items.risks: Directory enumeration across orgs; agents resolving to the wrong person.

verevon.exactGap: People side (SRC): org-core already serves GET /orgs/:id/members/search (name or email substring, active plus invited members, max 20 results, max 50 profile fetches), but the gateway never proxies it and nothing in the SPA calls it; the add-member picker instead lists every active org member from the gateway list_members route with no search box. Agent side (SRC): an org-wide agent registry already exists in the Application Plane (agentInstallationsForOrgForGateway, gateway GET /api/v1/agents/installations, ADR-0002, a presence-not-authority label surface) and the composer builds @-candidates from Space roster plus bound agents only, but nothing merges people and agents, and no agent-callable resolver returning ok/ambiguous/none exists in Model, Application or Control code (INF, from a negative grep of resolve_/lookup_/find_ patterns). The DM, group-room and guest targets the item names do not exist yet (Space kind is only personal/room/project/case), so a DM picker has no consumer today.
reuse: org-core searchMembers handler and MemberSuggestion type (restrict to active members before exposing)
gateway orgs/members.rs list_members (auth-core list-members, already returns name and email)
Application registry: Convex agentInstallationsForOrgForGateway and gateway list_org_agent_installations (ADR-0002)
SpaceRoomComposer MentionCandidate model (person|agent) and the Control RosterMember shape (subject_type user|service)
gateway authorized_org_id pattern so the org always comes from the session, never from the client
verevon.constraints: Plane ownership (SRC): people identity is auth-core/org-core (Auth Core is the sole membership authority); the cross-Space agent registry is owned by the Application Plane per ADR-0002, so a Control-owned combined directory conflicts with that ADR for the agent half. ADR-0002 says the registry answers presence, not authority: a resolver result must never imply the caller may invoke the agent, which still needs Control roster/decision for the specific Space. org-core members/search is service-authenticated with no per-user delegation and also returns invited emails, so it must be exposed only through the gateway with the session org and active-only filtering. Cross-org or external lookup needs the cross-org identity and privacy contract the UI research doc requires (SRC: VEREVON_UI_COWORK_RESEARCH_2026-08-13.md:128-132), so it must wait for F-t1-053. ZDR is not affected (names and emails only). The default ORG_MEMBERSHIP_LIMIT is 100 (SRC auth.ts:953-956), so client-side filtering of the existing list is enough at default scale.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not make Control the directory owner for agents. Slice 1 (S): add a search field to the existing add-member picker, or expose org-core members/search through a gateway route that forces the session org and returns active members only. Slice 2 (M): compose people (org-core/auth-core) and agents (Application registry) in the gateway, and expose the ok|ambiguous|none resolver as an agent tool through the gateway/capability path with presence-not-authority semantics. Defer external and guest lookup to the guest model.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged overall, but the people-search slice is S because org-core search and the roster list already exist; the agent resolver tool is the M part.
verevon.verdictReason: Recommendation is valid but two premises are wrong: a people search already exists in org-core (just unexposed and with an invited-email leak), and the plane owner for the agent half is the Application Plane (ADR-0002), not Control. Also depends on DMs and guests that do not exist.

items.title: Meeting intelligence with consent: long-form transcription and an authority-scoped recap saved as a Space document, under a deny-by-default per-meeting AI policy
items.summary: Build the meeting-intelligence MVP from uploaded recordings first, then live calls: long-form speech-to-text with speaker labels and timestamps in the Model Plane, transcript segments stored as Data Plane knowledge units (not room posts), and a recap (decisions, action items with owners, chapters, citations to segments) written back as an editable Space document. Gate it with a Control-owned per-meeting policy {ai_access off|transcript_only|full, privacy_mode, ephemeral or retained answers, managers, locked fields} checked before any ASR, agent or recap reads audio or transcript, announced to all participants, default-off when externals are present.
items.whyItMatters: Transcript and AI recap are table stakes in Teams, Slack and buzz, and the meeting-intelligence design (a meeting as a source type on existing retrieval, wiki and ZDR rails) is architecturally sound but has no code. Teams' consent controls must ship with it, not after.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Teams (REA): recap with notes, tasks, topics, chapters, speaker timeline, citations back to the recording and visibility derived from transcript access; Teams (REA): visible AI on/off, privacy mode that blocks Copilot and all agents, ephemeral versus retained answers by org policy, only selected people can change AI settings, admin-locked options shown as locked
others: Slack (DOC): notes become a canvas in the huddle
Buzz (SRC): transcript segments are ordinary chat messages in the meeting channel
Slack (DOC): announce to all when AI notes start, default off with external guests
Grok Bot (SRC, medium): per-meeting or blanket consent card for the agent and an admin visibility setting (MANAGERS or EVERYONE)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-03-02] 3 of 5 (Buzz, Slack, Teams); table-stakes. Citations, attendance report and content-bin report are Teams-only. [R-t1-03-03] 2 of 5 (Teams, Slack) for AI policy, differentiator; Grok Bot adds consent for agent attendance; admin-locked indicator is Teams-only.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-03-02] Audio to streaming or batch ASR with diarisation produces segments {speaker, t_start, t_end, text}; on meeting end a reasoning pass produces the recap with citations to segments; the recap is saved as an editable document or canvas in the room; action items become tasks only after human approval; recap visibility equals transcript visibility (no transcript access, no AI summary); attendance comes from roster events. [R-t1-03-03] Policy evaluated server-side before any agent or ASR reads meeting content. Enabling AI emits a system message to participants and a badge. Externals present means default off. Ephemeral answers are stored with a meeting-scoped TTL. Fields locked by an admin render as locked with the owner of the lock.

items.approach: [R-t1-03-02] Model Plane: add a long-form transcription job beside TranscribeSpeech in inference-core (self-hosted WhisperX plus diarisation for sovereign and ZDR tenants, cloud ASR otherwise) returning segments with speaker, start, end, text and language, exposed through a model-gateway job route. Data Plane v2: ingest segments as knowledge units of source kind meeting with speaker and timestamp metadata so existing dense, sparse and graph retrieval work unchanged. Recap: Model Plane reasoning with the Meeting Scribe rules, written back as a wiki page or Space document through Data Plane contracts; action items proposed as tasks behind the existing approval cards (SpaceApprovalPanel). Control Plane: private-until-shared visibility with attendees as the default audience and the this item (R-t1-03-03) policy as precondition. Frontend: a Meetings section in the Space cockpit (SpaceCockpit.tsx tab list has chat, work, knowledge, activity, agent, members), upload-recording flow and a recap viewer with citation links. Attendance from call roster events. [R-t1-03-03] Control Plane (apps/Control Plane/user-core, spaces package): policy storage with org default and admin lock, plus new effects such as space.meeting.transcribe and space.meeting.ai_read whose signed decisions carry purpose and privacy class per ADR-0001. Application Plane enforces per meeting and emits the announcement event to the Space activity feed. Model Plane ASR and agents must present an allow decision and refuse otherwise, failing closed like decide_content_route. Enforcement sits on the data: transcript and recap knowledge units carry the policy revision so retrieval cannot leak them through a chat copy. Ephemeral answers use a meeting-scoped TTL. Frontend: policy chip in the call bar and meeting card; reuse the admin-locked affordance on existing Space settings.

items.title: Retention policies for rooms, files and agent sessions, plus shared-Space deletion on the existing saga
items.summary: Add org and per-Space retention policies (keep, N days, ZDR) carried in Control's signed decision and enforced by per-plane sweepers that reuse the per-plane receipts of the Space deletion saga: room projections, Model Plane threads, messages and agent memory, sandbox-manager workspaces and process output, Data Plane documents bound to the Space, and notification feeds. Extend the saga from personal Spaces to shared Spaces with owner approval and write fencing. Legal hold overrides retention.
items.whyItMatters: Retention is a gating enterprise question and a GDPR storage-limitation duty. Verevon has the hardest part already (cross-plane receipts, legal hold) but only for personal Space deletion, and nothing between keep-forever and ZDR.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: slack

referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Retention: 3 of 5 (slack, teams, buzz doc); durable shared-space deletion: 1 of 5 (buzz). Common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Policy objects at org, workspace, channel and DM scope; the most specific wins unless the org locks it, with a member override for private rooms. A scheduled sweeper deletes expired items across stores via deletion receipts; policy changes are audited and may need owner approval. Deletion: request, frozen inventory digest, owner approval, write fence, resumable executor with checkpoints, abortable until destruction starts, final receipt.

items.title: Typed timeline entries: server-signed system messages, a card registry with a safe fallback, link previews through Quarry, and pointer embeds for artifacts
items.summary: Give Session Core entries a content_type plus payload, render by type through a card registry with a neutral unsupported-update fallback, and let the server emit typed system entries from Control and Application events (member added or removed, agent bound or paused, rename, history window). Add link previews fetched by Quarry with SSRF guards and stored as a snapshot so recipients never contact the third-party site, provider link cards classified in the browser, and an embed block that stores only {kind, id} for a canvas, list, record or file and renders it under the viewer's own grant with a request-access stub.
items.whyItMatters: Teams has 87+ typed system notices including agent added or removed, and buzz signs notices so clients cannot forge them; Verevon shows membership and binding changes only in a separate Activity tab. Pointer embeds keep artifacts under their own ACL instead of copying content into messages.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (typed previews with unknown and retired fallback cards); teams (87+ typed system notices incl. agent added or removed); buzz (relay-signed notices, sender-side link snapshots); Teams Loop (REA) for pointer embeds with their own ACL and a sharing warning; Grok Bot (SRC) for provider link-card classification
others: Slack typed cloud pickers as hardened child windows (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-01-10] Typed content 2 of 5 and system messages 2 of 5 (differentiators); link previews 3 of 5 (common) [R-t1-08-10] pointer embeds: 1 of 5, unique; provider cards and pickers: 2 of 5, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-01-10] Entry {content_type enum, payload oneof}; the preview projection is typed; the client renders a fallback card for unknown types and logs once per type. System entries {type, actor, subject, details} are emitted by the server from authority events and are never client-authored (buzz signs them with the relay key). Link preview: the sender side fetches under SSRF guards (private-IP block, redirect cap, 256 KB page and 2 MB image caps, per-host cooldown), extracts OG metadata, re-hosts a sanitized image and stores a signed snapshot with the message; recipients never contact the third-party site. Slack lets apps enrich unfurls. [R-t1-08-10] Message body contains an embed {artifact_kind, artifact_id}; the renderer fetches the artifact under the viewer's grant and subscribes to live updates; a viewer without access sees a request-access stub; pasting elsewhere reuses the same id; the share dialog warns when posting to an audience wider than the artifact ACL. Link cards use host-pattern to provider and path-pattern to kind tables and never fetch content.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-01-10] AppendMessageRequest carries role (user, assistant, system, tool), content and a metadata struct but no content_type; room posts render as markdown or plain text. Membership, grants and receipts appear in the separate Activity tab, not in the room timeline (checked in features/spaces: no member-added or agent-bound timeline rows). No link previews. Baseline had no record for typed content or system entries, so a final check of Session Core message conventions is still needed. [R-t1-08-10] Room posts cannot embed any artifact (chat artifacts are inline SSE payloads, not pointers to an independently authorized object). No link previews or provider cards in rooms; the baseline recorded attachments and link previews as absent in the room, and the integration-core provider actions are not offered as a picker (not re-verified).

items.approach: [R-t1-01-10] Model Plane proto: add content_type and a payload oneof (or a namespaced metadata.kind as an interim to avoid a breaking migration); existing rows default to text. Application Plane: project Control membership and binding events and Space lifecycle events into typed system entries appended under a server-only decision (clients cannot author them). Frontend: card registry (text, system notice, approval card, receipt, file, link preview, unknown fallback). Ingestion Plane: a Quarry fetch-preview endpoint (private-IP block, redirect cap, 256 KB and 2 MB caps, OG extract, re-hosted sanitized image) called by the gateway at send; snapshot stored on the entry; integration-corev2 providers can later supply richer unfurls. ZDR orgs may disable previews. Coordinate with category 12 (C-t1-12-012 typed transcript rows) and category 06 (C-t1-06-027 unfurling). [R-t1-08-10] Frontend Plane: an embed block type in room messages rendering canvas, list, record and file cards by id through the gateway under the viewer's decision; a pure client-side URL classifier for provider cards; pickers later through Ingestion integration-corev2 OAuth grants that never widen the owner ACL. Application Plane live updates reuse the existing realtime projection. Adopt the embed format inside the canvas and lists work, not as a separate product.
dependencies: Control and Application event feeds for membership and agent binding
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (entry schema) with Application Plane (system projection), Ingestion Plane (Quarry preview) and Frontend Plane (card registry)
items.risks: [R-t1-01-10] Schema migration of existing turns. Event-to-timeline consistency. SSRF and tracking-pixel leakage in previews; preview snapshots under ZDR; titles of private pages leaking through external unfurls. A decision card must not be confused with a Control approval of an effect. [R-t1-08-10] N+1 fetches on long timelines. A request-access stub must not leak titles or metadata to unauthorized viewers. Server-side unfurl would leak URLs, so keep classification client-side.

verevon.exactGap: AppendMessageRequest carries role, content and an opaque metadata Struct but no content_type, and the room timeline normalizes transcripts to user and assistant turns only (normalizeTranscriptTurns drops every other role) rendered as markdown or plain text, with the approval panel as the only inline typed card; typed rendering exists only in the Activity tab (ActivityRenderClass and lenses). There are no member-added, agent-bound or rename rows in the timeline or in Activity (activity-grammar has no membership class), no link previews and no pointer embeds; Quarry has an SSRF guard (dns_guard) and OpenGraph extraction and the gateway has a render-based scrape-preview route, but no light metadata-only fetch-preview endpoint.

verevon.constraints: Session Core owns the transcript and appends into a Space thread need a fresh Control append decision per human actor, so a server-signed system entry needs a new Control-issued system-append class and clients must not be able to author it. The room is a list of thread-posts (each a Session Core thread), not one continuous timeline, so membership and agent-state notices have no thread to live in. The gateway never dials third-party URLs (it forwards to Quarry), previews must be snapshots stored at send so recipients never contact the site, and ZDR rooms disable previews and snapshots. Pointer embeds render under the viewer's own grant and a request-access stub must not leak titles; embeds depend on the canvas and lists items existing first.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Change the system-notice design: do not append notices into Session Core threads via Application. Emit them as typed room-level feed rows owned by an Application projection sourced from Control membership and binding events, and reserve Session Core content_type or metadata.kind for in-thread cards (approval, receipt, link preview, embed). Keep unknown roles and kinds as a neutral fallback in the transcript normalizer instead of dropping them. For previews add a metadata-only fetch mode to Quarry rather than reusing the render-based scrape-preview route.

items.title: Guests and link invitations with mandatory expiry
items.summary: Introduce a guest principal type with memberships only in explicitly granted rooms, no directory or roster access and no agent invocation by default, invited through room-scoped invitations with a required expiry. Extend invitations with shareable links or codes (TTL, max uses, optional admin approval, stored terms acceptance) and a combined invite-to-org-and-room flow.
items.whyItMatters: Teams, Slack, QM and Buzz all support external collaborators; Verevon rosters only active org members, so a customer or contractor cannot be pulled into one room. Org invitations exist but cannot target a room or be shared as a link.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (guest tiers), buzz (invite codes), qm (mandatory guest expiry)
others: slack (single- vs multi-channel guests, admin approval queue)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: guests 4 of 5 (table-stakes); link invitations 2 of 5 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: principal.type in {internal, guest}. Guests get memberships only in granted rooms, cannot browse the directory, create rooms or see the roster, and by default cannot invoke agents; invitations require expires_at and expiry removes memberships through the normal membership-change path. Invite code = base64(org, room?, role, expires_at, max_uses, nonce) + HMAC; claim verifies HMAC and expiry, counts uses, records terms acceptance, then creates the membership through the normal Control path; claim is rate-limited (10 per minute in Buzz).

verevonToday.gap: Org email invitations exist, but there are no guests, no room-scoped invitations, no link or code invites with max uses, no approval queue, and no stored terms acceptance.

items.approach: Control Plane (auth-core, org-core, user-core): guest principal type, room-scoped guest invitation with mandatory expiry, and link invites with TTL, max uses and an optional room target and role; per-org approval policy. Agent turns in rooms with guests use the room audience in the Control decision so org-only knowledge is not retrieved. Guest seats flow to billing-core. Frontend: invite dialog on the room with a link option.

items.risks: Agent answers in a guest room can leak org knowledge; guest seat billing; ZDR and residency apply to guest data too; link invites leak easily, so keep a short TTL, max uses and admin revoke.

verevon.exactGap: Only org-level email invitations exist (SRC): the Better Auth organization plugin in auth-core with a 48 h default expiry, email-verification requirement and a rate-limited accept route, and a gateway invite limited to member/admin roles; invitation rows carry an unused teamId column and the auth event publishes an empty inviteCode. There is no guest principal (Control space_memberships only allows user or service subjects; Application room grants require an existing active org member and are hard-coded to role editor), no room-scoped invitation, no link or code invite with max uses, no approval queue and no stored terms acceptance. The product docs also state that external access needs its own cross-org identity and privacy contract before any invite list (SRC: VEREVON_UI_COWORK_RESEARCH_2026-08-13.md:128-132).
reuse: Better Auth invitation table and flow in auth-core (expiresAt already mandatory, status, inviterId; add a room target and a token for link invites)
sendInvitationEmail/buildInvitationLink and AcceptInvitationPage plus the accept-invitation rate limit
Control recipient-audience and Space decision machinery as the fence that keeps org-only knowledge out of guest rooms (ADR-0001 intersection rule)
