billing-core seat concept (not opened in this audit; verify before relying on it)
verevon.constraints: Auth Core is the sole org-membership authority (SRC: org-core/internal/http/server.go:122-128 comment), so guest identity belongs in auth-core, not in Application. A guest must NOT become a plain org member (INF): org-visible documents and the organization-room roster sync would then include them. Room membership writes today flow Application spaceMemberGrants -> declarative PUT to Control, and ReplaceMemberships revokes any managed (user) member not in the declared list (SRC repository.go:744-775), so a Control-created guest membership of subject_type user would be revoked on the next sync unless the guest uses a distinct subject_type or the sync is scoped by source. Control space_memberships CHECK allows only user and service (SRC 017 migration line 62). Agent turns in a guest room must use the room recipient audience so retrieval is narrowed (ADR-0001); I did not trace that Data Plane honors the audience for org-visible documents. ZDR and residency apply to guest data. The org membership cap defaults to 100 and would count guests unless modelled separately. Link invites are a mass-exposure path: short TTL, max uses, admin revoke, rate limit.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Add a decision gate before building: choose the guest identity model (separate principal type versus restricted org role) and write the cross-org identity and privacy contract the UI research doc requires. Make one writer own room membership (see F-t1-054 source tagging) or give guests their own subject_type excluded from the Application declarative sync. Reuse the Better Auth invitation for the email path (expiry is already mandatory) and add the room target; ship link or code invites as a later slice. Keep guests out of the org-room sync and out of org-visible Data Plane documents.
verevon.effortNote: L to XL: no guest primitive exists in any plane, and the work spans an identity-model decision, auth-core, a Control membership schema and sync change, Data Plane visibility treatment, billing seats and agent-audience fencing.
verevon.verdictReason: Recommendation stays valid and the org-invitation base is correctly described, but the approach omits the identity-model gate and the declarative-sync clobber, and underestimates effort; keep it in the late wave.

items.title: Teams and sub-groups with source-tracked membership; mentionable groups
items.summary: Add a team concept to Control (owners, members, visibility) where a team grant expands into room memberships tagged with their source, so removing someone from a team removes only team-derived grants. Later add team-level mentions (server-side expansion at send) once Space notifications exist.
items.whyItMatters: Teams are the core of the Teams half of the vision: orgs organise people into teams with their rooms. Today there is no team concept, only flat org membership and per-room lists. Teams are also the prerequisite for SCIM group sync, team-level agent context and group-based agent access.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams
others: qm (team contributes read-only resources to a turn only under a membership rule)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: teams 2 of 5 (teams, qm), mentionable groups 2 of 5 (teams, slack); common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: team(id, org_id, name, visibility), team_members(team_id, principal, role owner|member), team_rooms(team_id, room_id). Joining a team grants membership in its standard rooms; private rooms keep their own roster. Mentions: the server expands @tag into the member list at send and fans out through the notification service with per-recipient permission checks. QM teamsForTurn includes a team layer only if the actor is on the team AND the room is configured for it.

evidence: apps/Application Plane/conversation-core/conversation-core-go/internal/http/server.go:92 (ticket teams are support routing only)
apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/schema.ts:556-562 (comment anticipates team rooms as kind room, but no team table)
verevonToday.gap: No team or sub-group concept, no source tracking on memberships, no group mentions; Space events produce no notifications, so group mentions have nothing to ride on.

items.approach: Control Plane (org-core and user-core): teams as a membership source; a team grant expands into space_memberships rows tagged with source, and removal only clears that source. Application Plane: team directory projection and, later, tag definitions; notification-core allowlist extended for mention events. Team resources reach agents only through owner-plane grants, never widened by team membership. Agents in a mentionable group must be opt-in.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane
items.risks: Team-derived plus manual membership needs source tracking or removing someone from a team will wrongly remove a manual grant. Broadcast mentions to agents can trigger many paid model turns.

verevon.exactGap: No usable team concept exists, but there is dormant scaffolding (SRC): auth-core defines team and team_member tables plus invitation.team_id in its Drizzle schema, the organization plugin config does not enable teams, and nothing reads those tables; resource_grants reserves a team subject_type in its CHECK constraint while the ACL repository rejects any non-user subject ("MVP is user-only"). Room membership has no source or provenance (space_memberships has only a free-text granted_by that the Application sync overwrites), and the only sync is a declarative full replace from Application, so team-derived memberships would be revoked as stale. There are no user-groups or group mentions in the gateway, Convex or the Space UI, and a grep found no Space-originated consumer in notification-core (INF), so group mentions have nothing to ride on.
reuse: auth-core team and team_member tables (enable the Better Auth teams option) as the team store
resource_grants subject_type team slot (already allowed by the DB CHECK) for team-level resource shares
Control space_memberships plus ReplaceMemberships (add a source dimension)
Convex spaceMemberGrants intent record and syncRoomMembersForGateway
spaceAgents triggerModes (mention|group) for agent trigger semantics
verevon.constraints: Auth Core owns membership and org-core deliberately does not mount membership or policy mutations (SRC server.go:122-128), so the team store belongs in auth-core with expansion into space_memberships in user-core; the item names org-core and user-core. The membership writer must be decided first (INF from SRC repository.go:744-775 and spaceMembers.ts:243): Application declares only manual user grants with managed_subject_types [user], so any team-derived Control membership is deactivated on the next room sync unless the declaration carries it or the sync is scoped to source=manual. Team membership never widens an owner-plane ACL (ADR-0001). Notifications: Space mention delivery does not exist, so group mentions stay a later phase as the item says. Agents in a mentionable group must be opt-in because one broadcast can trigger many paid turns.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Start from the existing auth-core team and team_member tables instead of a new Control concept. Decide the single writer of room membership first: either carry a source per member in the Application declaration (manual or team:<id>) or let Control own writes with a source column on space_memberships and scope ReplaceMemberships to source=manual. Use the reserved team subject_type in resource_grants for team-level sharing.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: the dormant tables save a little, but the membership-writer decision and the sync change keep it L.
verevon.verdictReason: The gap is real, but the claim that no team concept exists is slightly wrong (dormant auth-core tables and a reserved grant subject exist) and the plane split should name auth-core for the team store and call out the sync clobber.

items.title: Personal sidebar organisation: stars, custom sections, per-group sort, hide, mute, drag-and-drop, computed system sections and cross-org badges
items.summary: Give each user a synced sidebar preference document (stars, custom sections, per-group sort, hidden refs, mute) edited with drag-and-drop and a batch mode, plus computed system sections over the same summaries (Agent runs, Waiting for approval, Unread, Muted) that can be toggled off, and a rate-limited stale-room suggestion. Add a per-org attention summary so the workspace switcher shows cross-org badges, with keyboard switching. Ship layout changes behind a flag with a switch-back.
items.whyItMatters: Sidebar organisation is table stakes in four references and becomes necessary as soon as directory, DMs and team rooms add more conversations per person; today the groups are fixed and unread is browser-local.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (sections), slack (workspace rail); Buzz (sort per group, synced sections and stars, dnd-kit sorting, More-unread pill); Teams for computed system sections and switch-back
others: Grok Bot (hide from sidebar, batch move/hide/delete for agents)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-02-12] sections 2 of 5 (teams, slack; common); account and workspace switching 4 of 5 (table-stakes, partly present) [R-t1-12-04] organisation 4 of 5 (Buzz, Grok Bot, QM, Slack; table-stakes); system sections and view modes 1 of 5 (Teams; unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-02-12] user_sidebar(user_id, org_id, sections[{id, name, emoji, sort, filter, items[]}], muted[], favorites[]) with keyboard-accessible drag between sections; stale suggestion = rooms with no visit in N days, excluding dont_suggest entries, rate-limited to once per day. Switcher: client keeps a list of {account, tenant, session}, one cheap unread badge per tenant from a per-tenant summary endpoint, Ctrl/Cmd+1..9 and next/previous, per-tenant sign-out clears only that tenant's local data. [R-t1-12-04] Per-user blob {stars:[ref], sections:[{id,name,refs[]}], sort:{group -> alpha|recent|priority}, hidden:[ref]} stored server-side and synced; groups render in fixed order, then user sections; sortable lists with a keyboard sensor; an IntersectionObserver on unread rows outside the viewport drives a "More unread" pill; selection mode with shift-range and bulk actions. Teams: system folders RECENT/MUTED/MEETING_CHATS as computed views toggled in settings, and a switch-back modal that preserves custom sections.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/core/components/sidebar/CoreSidebarSpacesPanel.tsx:104-232 (fixed groups plus a text filter)
apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/auth/auth.ts:835-837 and :942-948 (multiSession up to 10, organizationLimit 5)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/core/components/sidebar/CoreSidebarSpacesPanel.tsx:104-232 and 281-321 (org room pinned first, thread pinned/unread/working dots, filter box)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/lib/space-unread.ts (unread mirrors Application Plane read markers, but only for the open room)
verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-02-12] No sections, favorites, ordering or mute; the switcher has no cross-org unread badges, keyboard switching or tenant marker. Unread is browser-local even within one org (UI baseline), so a badge has nothing server-side to read. [R-t1-12-04] No user stars, custom sections, sort modes, drag-and-drop, hide or bulk actions, no filters or system sections, and unread dots exist only for the room open in this browser.

items.approach: [R-t1-02-12] Application Plane: per-user sidebar preferences and visit timestamps, plus a server-side unread and attention projection per org and member. Frontend: sections with drag ordering and mute in CoreSidebarSpacesPanel; badges and Ctrl+1..9 in the WorkspaceSwitcher. Each org's badge must come from that org's own projection (no cross-plane joins). [R-t1-12-04] Application Plane owns a per-user preference document (refs only, no room names, so retention and ZDR are not touched) read and written through typed gateway actions. Frontend Plane renders groups and computed sections from the conversation summaries, with the drag-and-drop and selection mode. Priority sort waits on the salience model already used by the Activity grammar. Note: package.json has no drag-and-drop or virtualisation library and runs Solid 2.0 RC, so check compatibility of solid-dnd or build keyboard-first sorting on existing primitives.
dependencies: Room discovery (F-t1-048 (R-t1-02-02)) for more rooms per user
Run and approval state present in conversation summaries (for system sections)
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (preferences) with Frontend Plane (sidebar UI)
items.risks: [R-t1-02-12] Section names are user content; ZDR orgs may require that they are not logged. [R-t1-12-04] Low authority risk, since preferences are per user and touch no Space ACL. Solid 2 RC library compatibility. Too many default sections clutters the list.

verevon.exactGap: The Spaces sidebar (CoreSidebarSpacesPanel.tsx:30-232) has fixed groups (Channels with the org room pinned first, Personal Space, All conversations of the selected room) plus a text filter, with no stars, custom sections, ordering, hide, mute or room-level unread badge, and the org WorkspaceSwitcher (CoreNavbar.tsx:672-729) has no cross-org badge or keyboard switching. A reusable organiser already exists for chat threads (ChatSidebarOrganizer.tsx and chat-organization.ts: custom projects, assignments, group/sort/filter views, native HTML5 drag with an accessible Move menu, a zod-typed action reducer) but it is browser-local (localStorage) and mounted for chat only. The item's 'unread is browser-local' premise is imprecise: the per-room marker is server-side in Convex, but sidebar unread dots come from a browser store populated only for rooms whose page was opened this session, and no cross-room or cross-org unread or attention aggregate exists.
reuse: ChatSidebarOrganizer native drag-and-drop with the accessible Move menu, and its zod-typed ChatOrganizationAction reducer, promoted to a server-synced preference document (this removes the 'no drag-and-drop library' concern)
listOrganizations and switchActiveOrganization behind the existing WorkspaceSwitcher for the cross-org list
activity-grammar.ts salience classes as the existing basis for a priority sort and computed system sections
Convex own-row, refs-only pattern (spaceReadMarkers, spacePresence) for the per-user preference document
server-pinned thread flag already relayed by the presentation route and the sidebar unread dot component
verevon.constraints: Each gateway request resolves exactly one authorised org (authorized_org_id from the active org), so cross-org badges need a deliberate multi-org read path that checks membership per target org and never mixes two orgs' data in one response (tenant and ZDR partition). Hide, mute and sort are presentation only and must never widen or narrow Space access; mute must be a notification preference distinct from agent pause. The preference document should store spaceRefs and ids, not room names, and live in the Application Plane as a per-user own-row record. Any server-computed attention summary must come from Application-owned read markers plus owner-plane events or APIs (approvals live in Model Plane), not DB reads. Solid 2.0 RC means prefer the existing native-drag pattern over a new library. The doc non-goals mention notification polish, which makes mute and system sections the least contentious part.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Correct the premise: unread is server-backed per room, so the missing dependency is a per-user, per-org attention summary (rooms with unread, waiting approvals), not 'server-side unread state'. First slice: stars, custom sections, hide, mute and per-group sort for Space rooms by promoting the chat organiser's pattern and action reducer to a synced Convex preference document; computed system sections (Unread, Waiting for approval, Agent runs, Muted) on top of the attention summary; cross-org badges and Ctrl+1..9 as a separate later item that needs the multi-org read path.
verevon.effortNote: M holds for the room-organisation slice reusing the existing organiser; the attention aggregate and cross-org badges are a separate L, so bundled it is L.
verevon.verdictReason: Status is partial for rooms and the pattern already exists for chat; the unread premise and the drag-and-drop concern are wrong, and cross-org badges need a different dependency than the item names.

items.title: Agent task tracker: Needs-input state, per-task threads and unread in the Work tab
items.summary: Give each agent task a visible state (working, needs input, done) with a note, a task-scoped thread beside the room and per-task unread, and project it into the Space Work tab and the activity inbox. Extend the capability-core task registry with a space_ref, a thread_ref and a needs_input state, keeping agent-owned tasks distinct from human-owned list items but linkable.
items.whyItMatters: A human should see exactly which agent task is waiting for them, which is the Grok Bot behaviour the vision asks for. Verevon already shows runs awaiting approval, but nothing says an agent is blocked on a question or lets a person answer in a task thread.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (SRC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Task {id, title, state: working|needs_input|done, note, created_at, done_at, seen_done_at}; each task has a sub-thread id; a message sent with task_id routes to the agent about that task; a panel shows unread replies and done-but-unseen tasks, and the tasks panel is asynchronous.

verevonToday.gap: Per-thread orchestration todos exist, and /v1/tasks proxies the capability-core task registry (org-scoped, status filter, create, patch, cancel) with states created, assigned, blocked and completed and an assignee, but types.go has no space or thread field (the handler may store more). The Work tab lists runs and shows awaiting_approval as a critical needs-a-human state. There is no free-form Needs-input state, no per-task thread or unread, and no room-level task list.

items.approach: Model Plane capability-core owns task state: add space_ref, thread_ref and a needs_input substate to the task registry and pass space_ref through the /v1/tasks proxy as the cron list already does. Application Plane projects task state into the Space Work tab and the activity inbox. Frontend renders task threads beside the room and per-task unread, and reuses the Activity grammar so a waiting task reads the same in Work and Activity. Messages posted in a task thread route to the task session.
dependencies: Adoption plan S4.5 unified Work cockpit
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: Overlap with Lists (F-t1-058 (R-t1-08-06)); keep agent-owned tasks separate from human-owned list items and link them by ref. The task registry semantics (types.go describes a seeded catalog) need confirming.

verevon.exactGap: A durable task registry already exists (capability-core TasksHandler over the tasks table: run_id, kind, title, assignee, priority and a free-form status that PATCH accepts, produced by the cron sweeper and the API, proxied by model-gateway /v1/tasks), but it is org-scoped with no space_ref or thread_ref, no Control decision on read or write, no agent-run producer, no caller in verevonv3, and no needs-input state or agent pause to feed one; the internal/tasks/types.go the item cites is only a seeded read-only catalog. The Work tab (SpaceWorkPanel) lists runs and schedules with awaiting_approval as its only needs-a-human state, per-thread todos live in session-core, and unread is a room-level last-read marker rather than per-task.
evidence: apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/api/workplane_apis.go:768-800 (PATCH accepts any non-empty status or assignee)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/cron/sweeper.go:244 (only internal producer of task rows)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/tasks/types.go:1-30 (seeded read-only catalog, no space or thread field)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/http_routes.rs:345-347,5341-5360 (task proxy forwards org_id and status only)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/grpc.rs:2399-2450 (gRPC CreateTask and ListTasks proxy to capability-core)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/migrations/0004_tasks_cron_hooks_skills_memory.sql:17-40 (tasks table: run_id, status text, no space column)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/lib/space-unread.ts:23-45 (unread vs a room read marker)
apps/Model Plane (grep: no needs_input, input_required or ask-user pause anywhere; no /v1/tasks caller in verevonv3 src or gateway)
reuse: capability-core tasks table and TasksHandler (status is free text, so a needs_input value needs no migration; run_id already links a task to a run, its thread and Space)
session-core threads and runs carrying Space context, so a task thread can be an ordinary Space thread created under a Control thread decision
session-core todos and plans for per-thread task steps
activity-grammar RUN_STATUS and buildSpaceWork plus SpaceWorkPanel gap rendering
Convex space read marker for unread
gateway run_watchers for notify-when-finished
verevon.constraints: Task rows are org-scoped and the list is not filtered by Space authority, so adding a free space_ref column that any org caller can set or read would leak private rooms; follow the Space cron pattern (Control decision on create, space_ref only as a filter, never a grant) or derive the Space from run_id through Session Core, and project to the Work tab only after a Space read decision. State stays in the Model Plane and Application Plane only projects it. A real needs-input state needs a Model-side clarification pause that does not exist, so this is not a frontend-only change. ZDR runs must not persist task content.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Reword to: link tasks to runs and threads through run_id plus a Control-bound space_ref, add needs_input as a status value together with a Model-side ask-the-human pause, and reuse the Space thread of the run and the existing todos before inventing per-task threads. Keep agent-owned tasks separate from human Lists (F-t1-058) and link by ref. Remove the quick-win label.
verevon.effortNote: Was M and a quick win. There is no agent producer, no Space authority on tasks and no clarification pause, so L.
verevon.verdictReason: The cited file is a seeded catalog; the live registry is different and more capable, but it has no Space authority. The item should say what exists (registry, status text, run link) and place the real work on authority and the pause primitive.

items.title: Artifact sharing: edit role, Space-as-subject grants, general access and access requests
items.summary: Extend the single resource_grants authority in Control Plane user-core with an edit role, a Space subject type (evaluated as the Space decision intersected with the resource grant), a general-access setting that defaults off per org, and an access-request flow with a human-only approve action. Extend ShareDialog to cover canvases, files and artifacts, not just documents. Phase 1 (edit role plus Space subject) must land together with the canvas and file library.
items.whyItMatters: Every artifact type in a room needs its own grants so sharing into a Space never widens the owner ACL, and the access-request loop routes the decision through a human owner. Without an edit role other members cannot co-author the canvas.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (SRC): Google-Docs-style dialog with request access and approve or decline from chat after an owner/manager check
others: Slack canvas sharing (DOC): view/edit grants independent of conversation membership, mentions notify only people with access
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 4 of 5 sources; table-stakes
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grant rows {resource, subject (user|group|space), role (view|edit), granted_by}; a general_access enum on the resource; request_access creates a pending item delivered to the owner; the decide endpoint verifies the decider manages the resource's home scope, then grants (never downgrading an existing higher role) or sends a deduplicated decline notice; mentions inside an artifact notify only subjects with access.

verevonToday.gap: Shares are view-only and user-only: create_share hard-codes role view and subject_type user (shares.rs:114-115), the list and revoke routes are keyed to documents, and the only other surface is a shared-with-me list. There is no edit role, no group or Space subject, no general access, no access-request or approval flow, and no sharing for non-document artifacts.

items.approach: Control Plane user-core: add role edit, subject_type space (grant effective only when the current Space decision also allows, per the ADR intersection rule at SPACE_AUTHORITY_ADR_2026-08-13.md:64-70), a general_access field defaulting to restricted, and an access_requests table whose approve action is human-only and not model-eligible. Gateway shares.rs: generalize routes from documents/{id}/shares to resource_type and resource_id. Frontend: extend ShareDialog and deliver requests through the activity inbox (category 05). Keep resource_grants as the only grant store.
dependencies: Resource types for canvas and file artifacts (F-t1-015 (R-t1-08-01), F-t1-013 (R-t1-08-03))
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (user-core)
items.risks: A Space-subject grant must not become an ACL-widening path. Link access conflicts with ZDR and data residency, so keep it off by default per org. Hidden dependency: F-t1-015 (R-t1-08-01) and F-t1-013 (R-t1-08-03) cannot safely ship without phase 1.

verevon.exactGap: Control resource_grants already supports role edit (DB CHECK, AclRepository normalizeRole, authz check returns view or edit) and reserves a team subject, so only the gateway shares.rs hard-coding of document, user and view (lines 111-115) and the document-only, view-only ShareDialog behind the ownership gate stand between the UI and an edit role; "document" is the only ownable type in resource_taxonomy.json, a space subject_type does not exist (CHECK allows user and team), and no access-request flow exists (negative grep). Blocking finding (SRC): user-core mounts POST/DELETE /authz/grant and GET /authz/grants behind requireVerifiedAuthzDelegation, which only admits GET /authz/visible and /authz/check with a v2 ZDR-bounded delegation, while the gateway signs v1 delegation for every user-core call, so the share write path is fenced off in Control today ("Disabled until verified delegation exists" in server.go). Documents already have a Space edge (documents.space_ref plus Control retrieval decision), which overlaps with a Space-subject grant for documents.
reuse: resource_grants and AclRepository (edit role, team subject slot, ListVisible and Check)
authz facade /visible and /check with the Data Plane v2 delegation clients
documents.space_ref and Control retrieval-decision for Space-bound documents (spaces.rs space_knowledge)
Control space_memberships in the same user-core database for a Space-to-member join without cross-plane access
ShareDialog, ownership-gate honesty gate and the shared-with-me list
ADR-0001 intersection rule as the evaluation contract
verevon.constraints: ADR-0001: effective access is Space decision AND recipient audience AND owner-plane authorization, and Space membership never widens a resource ACL, so a Space-subject grant must only narrow or co-require, never add an independent path (SRC). Both resource_grants and space_memberships live in user-core, so the membership join is possible in-plane, but Space privacy, entitlement, ZDR and legal-hold conditions cannot be evaluated by a visible-ids query, so the owner plane needs a Control read-time decision as retrieval already does (INF). Every new resource type (canvas, file, artifact) must be classified in resource_taxonomy.json and its Rust mirror in retrieval-engine passes a parity lint, otherwise ValidateUserGrant rejects it. The access-request approve action must be human-only: grant a Control scope that no agent or Model service principal holds. General access conflicts with ZDR and residency, so default off per org. Agents (service principals) must never gain access through a Space subject grant. Grant administration requires the owning service to prove the actor administers the resource (SRC authz_facade.go:29-33 comment).
verevon.approachAdjustment: First unblock the write path: either add a verified resource-owner delegation (owner plane proves the actor administers the resource) or a dedicated gateway-to-Control grant-admin scope, because POST/DELETE /authz/grant and GET /authz/grants are currently rejected by requireVerifiedAuthzDelegation. Then expose the edit role (Control already supports it; only shares.rs:114-115 hard-codes view), add subject_type space with a CHECK migration, classify new resource types in the taxonomy with the Rust mirror, and build access requests on the activity inbox. For documents reuse documents.space_ref rather than duplicating it with Space-subject grants. Generalize the gateway routes to resource_type and resource_id only after the owner planes for canvas and files exist.
verevon.effortNote: M to L: the grant write surface is fenced off in Control and needs a new reviewed delegation mode, the taxonomy has a Go/Rust parity lint, and Space-subject evaluation needs a Control read-time decision. Drop the quick-win flag.
verevon.verdictReason: Premise "shares are view-only" is incomplete: the edit role already exists in Control and the real blocker is the disabled grant write surface; Space-as-subject partly duplicates documents.space_ref. Keep, but re-scope and raise effort.

items.title: Typed room records and Lists: one revisioned work-object substrate with a table view, assignees and item threads
items.summary: Build a generic Space record primitive (stable id, namespaced type, body, prev-revision CAS, idempotent resubmit) in the Application Plane, then ship Lists on top of it: typed columns, a table view first (board later), assignees, saved views and an item thread. Agents create and update records through a Model Plane tool that proposes, with authority-bearing fields staying human-only.
items.whyItMatters: Slack and Teams both give rooms lists, and a list is the natural place to assign work to humans and agents and see status, which is the core of humans and agents cooperating on work. One substrate avoids building tasks, decisions and checklists separately and keeps edits out of chat unread counts.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack Lists (DOC) for the user model; Buzz NIP-AR (SRC) for the record substrate
others: Teams Lists, Planner and Wiki tabs (REA)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: lists: 3 of 5, common; typed-record substrate: 1 of 5, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Record = full snapshot {id (stable UUID), home_space, type (namespaced), title, body JSON, op (create|update|move|delete|restore), prev revision, optional root thread}; tables heads(id to head) and revisions; head advance is an atomic CAS on prev; resubmitting an accepted revision is idempotent; revisions never count toward unread or notifications; read access equals the room decision. A list is a record collection with a column schema {name, type: text|select|people|date|checkbox}; views store filter, sort, group and an optional default flag; assignment emits an activity item to the assignee; add message to list copies a message ref into an item.

verevonToday.gap: No Space-scoped record type, list or board. Planner documents in Convex are keyed by a legacy workspaceId (an ADR resource-local partition) and orchestration todos are per thread. Tickets are a separate route unlinked from Spaces. Humans cannot edit tasks in the room and there are no assignees, views or item threads.

items.approach: Application Plane (Convex) owns space_records and space_record_revisions keyed by spaceRef with a registered schema per record type and prev-CAS; Control read and write decisions gate every query and mutation. Do not create another generic project authority (ADR row 84 treats the Convex projects table as a migration candidate), so records hang off the Space aggregate. Frontend: Lists tab in SpaceCockpit, table view first, board later. Model Plane: list read and update tools calling the Application API under the run's delegated decision. Assignment events feed the planned activity inbox; allow linking a ticket ref into a list item.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane
items.risks: Scope creep toward a full Planner; ship one table view and a few field types first. Generic schemas drift, so keep a registry of record types shared by UI and agent tools.

verevon.exactGap: No Space-scoped record, list or board exists: convex-core has no space_records tables (the Space tables are spaces, bindings, lifecycle, deletion, grants, readMarkers, audiences, presence), spaces.rs routes 649-731 have no records route, and the cockpit tabs are chat, work, knowledge, activity, agent, members. Only adjacent scaffolding exists: plannerDocuments (workspaceId-keyed BlockSuite metadata with no gateway or frontend consumer), thread-scoped Model Plane todos (todo.rs; read-only in the chat run panel with a status-update proxy), org-scoped capability-core /api/v1/tasks, and support tickets with saved ticket-views. The item's agent-write path is not a simple tool: Control currently supports exactly one agent owner action (tickets.create), so a records write is a new owner-action vertical.
reuse: Convex spaceRef-keyed projection pattern with service key plus requireGatewayMember (spaceReadMarkers.ts, spacePresence.ts, spaces.ts setInstructionsForGateway)

Control effect-policy pattern for new record read and write effects: a deny-by-default *_entitled column on space_effect_policies plus a decision issuer in user-core/internal/spaces (migrations 019-028)
Model Plane Todo state vocabulary (pending, in_progress, blocked, completed, cancelled; blocked_by; assignee user or agent) as the item status model
ticket-views saved-view routes in tickets.rs as the shape of saved views
activity-grammar.ts verb/object/outcome grammar for record-change rows in the Space Activity tab
SpaceCockpit tab list as the host for a Lists tab
verevon.constraints: Convex does not evaluate Space roles (spaces.ts says Space roles are not a Convex-tracked concept; the gateway verifies live Control membership and Convex only re-verifies org membership with the service key), so 'Control decisions gate every query and mutation' must be implemented as gateway-side Control decisions for new record read/write effects, not inside convex-core. Records are content, so the new table must join the Space deletion owner-receipt flow and the ZDR rule, unlike presence and read markers which are content-free. ADR rows 84-85 forbid a second generic project authority and treat planner workspaceId as a resource-local partition, so records must hang off spaceRef and not reuse plannerDocuments, workspaceId or the Convex projects table. Assignees must be Control subject ids (space_memberships allows user and service subjects); ticket or document links must be refs whose access is rechecked by the owner plane on read, since Space access never widens an owner ACL. Model proposes, owner executes: an agent may only propose record changes, and Control resolves a single supported owner action today (model_action_view.go), with the browser Model allowlist still empty.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Ship human-edited records first (table view, typed columns, assignees, saved views, per-record thread later) with gateway-side Control decisions, and take the agent create/update path out of this item: it needs a new owner-action vertical (schema hash, run-bound decision with payload digest, owner verifier, approval continuation) like tickets.create. Reuse the Todo status vocabulary instead of inventing a new one, register the table in the Space deletion flow, and keep authority-bearing fields human-only.
verevon.effortNote: L holds only for the human-edited table, assignees and saved views; the agent write path is a separate L-to-XL vertical blocked on the S2 owner-action framework, so bundling it makes this XL.
verevon.verdictReason: Status is absent (confirmed in schema, route table and cockpit tabs), but the approach misstates how agents write records and where Space authority is enforced, and bundles an owner-action vertical into a table feature.

items.title: Do not disturb, quiet-hours schedules and urgent break-through, visible to agents
items.summary: Add a per-user attention state {dnd_until, schedules [{days, start, end, tz}], vip subjects} to notification-core and gate the router on it: while in DND, non-critical signals from non-VIP actors are stored for the inbox only and do not go to push or the OS, then flush when DND ends. Agents classify approval requests by urgency in capability-core, with a per-agent daily cap and an owner-configurable limit on critical break-through. Expose a coarse 'can I interrupt now' answer to agents, not the schedule itself.
items.whyItMatters: Agents work around the clock. Without DND they will page humans at night, and push (F-t1-035 (R-t1-05-05)) should not ship before this gate. It also helps the agents: one that can check whether a human is interruptible can defer a non-urgent ask instead of blocking a run.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (manual pause, schedule, admin default hours, VIP and urgent break-through); Teams for urgent messages and meeting auto-DND
others: Teams (priority contacts, urgent messages, auto-DND in meetings)
Buzz (explicitly has none; spec defers DND)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Slack combines a manual pause, a recurring schedule, admin default hours, a VIP override and a once-a-day 'notify anyway' urgent break-through (DOC). Teams adds urgent messages and priority contacts that pass DND and automatic DND in meetings (REA). Router rule: if the user is in DND, the signal is not critical and the actor is not VIP, store it in the inbox only and do not deliver to OS or push; queued items flush when DND ends; urgent break-through is rate-limited per sender.

verevonToday.gap: No DND, quiet hours or schedule exists in Spaces or notification-core (channels.go holds only org-level event-by-channel configuration). Quiet hours are named as part of S4.4, whose current source state is the delivery attempt state machine and a disabled-by-default worker.

items.approach: Application Plane (notification-core): attention-state table and a router gate placed after the F-t1-008 (R-t1-05-04) preference checks. Model Plane (capability-core): add an urgency class to approval and agent-awaiting signals, plus a per-agent daily critical cap. Frontend Plane: DND toggle, schedule editor and VIP list in Settings. Expose DND to agents only through a narrow 'interruptible now' read so the schedule itself is not disclosed to every room member's agents.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane
items.risks: Urgent-flag abuse by agents (cap per agent per day, owner-configurable); disclosing a user's schedule to agents or room members; queued items must flush once and in order.

alreadyPlanned.where: S4.4 quiet hours: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md (execution tracker, line 226) and the baseline note 'Quiet hours are planned in S4.4'

verevon.exactGap: Control user-core already stores a per-user NotificationSettings.QuietHours {enabled, start, end} (default off, 22:00-08:00) and a manual profile availability status (online/busy/away/offline, labelled as helpdesk behaviour), but nothing enforces or exposes them: the frontend has no quiet-hours UI and notification-core's only gate is a per-event opt-out (WithPreferenceGate, IsNotificationEnabled) with no time window, DND, VIP or urgency class. No Space event producers reach notification-core either (the sender allow-list is gateway 'notification.created' for the delegated user and capability-core run_completed/run_failed), and a gate-suppressed request is stored as suppressed and returns before dispatch, so it neither reaches push nor creates an inbox row.
reuse: user-core NotificationSettings and QuietHours (GET/PUT /api/v1/settings/notifications) as the source of truth to extend with timezone, days, dnd_until and VIP
notification-core WithPreferenceGate seam in Accept (service.go isNotificationEnabled) as the enforcement point, and the existing suppressed status
notification-core identity_sync NATS consumer as the pattern for projecting a user attention setting from Control into notification-core
AccountSettingsPage Availability section as the UI host and the existing profile status field
activity-grammar.ts salience classes (critical, attention, normal, muted) as the urgency vocabulary for approval and awaiting signals
verevon.constraints: DND is a person-level attribute that spans organisations, while notification-core rows and every Space or Model event are org-scoped, so keep the source of truth in Control user-core and project it into notification-core by event or API, never by cross-plane DB read. The existing gate is binary (suppressed or sent) and drops the inbox row too, so DND needs a tri-state (deliver, inbox-only, deferred) and a flush path; the delivery queue is off by default and rejects ZDR requests, so flush depends on finishing the S4.4 ledger (F-t1-060). Urgency must be set by the trusted producer (gateway or capability-core), not by the agent, with a per-agent cap; the 'interruptible now' answer to agents must be a narrow server-side read bound to the run's delegated subject that does not disclose the schedule or cross orgs. Quiet hours are already named in S4.4, and space-defenition.md lists 'notification polish' in its non-goals, so this is planned but only partly aligned with the stated non-goal.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Start from the existing user-core quiet-hours setting instead of a new attention-state table: add timezone (the profile already has one), days, dnd_until and VIP, project it into notification-core, and add the gate after the preference check with a deliver/inbox-only/defer decision. Sequence it after the Space notification producers (F-t1-008) exist, because there is nothing Space-specific to gate today, and fold the deferred flush into the single S4.4 ledger rather than a second queue.
verevon.effortNote: M holds for settings, gate and UI; the flush rides on the S4.4 ledger (F-t1-060) and the producers are separate items.
verevon.verdictReason: The item says no quiet hours exist, but a stored-and-unenforced per-user quiet-hours setting and a profile availability status already exist in Control; the build should extend them and respect the person-level versus org-scoped split.

items.title: Finish the S4.4 delivery ledger and add a content-free missed-activity digest
items.summary: Generalise notification-core's lease-based delivery-attempt ledger into the S4.4 Space delivery ledger: idempotency keys, max-age expiry, bounded retries, and delivery errors reported back to the agent run that produced the message. Then add an email channel and a per-user digest (hourly or daily) that auto-pauses after inactivity and, for ZDR orgs, carries counts and links only.
items.whyItMatters: The ledger is the foundation for push, email digests, scheduled agent output and the future Channel Plane without losing or duplicating messages. The digest pulls absent humans back when agents are blocked on them, cutting approval latency.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (delivery outbox and morning digest)
others: Buzz (content-free mention outbox bridged by an operator)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Outbox: 2 of 5 sources, differentiator; digest: 2 of 5, common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM's DeliveryStore does enqueue, claimPending and ack with idempotency keys, max-age expiry and 5 retries, and reports undeliverable errors back to the source session; its personal morning digest runs on a managed schedule that auto-pauses when the person is inactive. Teams-style missed-activity email summarises unread mentions and activity. Outbox row: id, idempotency_key, destination, source_ref, status, attempts, lease_until, with a reaper for stale leases.

verevonToday.gap: notification-core already has a leased delivery-attempt state machine (pending, claimed, sent_unconfirmed, acknowledged, failed, unknown) whose worker is disabled by default, but the Space delivery ledger is only a named gap (delivery_ledger_not_built) and the plan's tracker still lists durable feed reconciliation, provider and ZDR proof and HA as open. There is no email channel for Space events and no digest of any kind.

items.approach: Application Plane: extend notification-core's attempt ledger into the S4.4 Space ledger, keeping its semantics (provider acceptance is not confirmation; ambiguous outcomes stay 'unknown'; ZDR attempts content-free). Add idempotency keys and a reply-to-source error path for agent runs. Model Plane (capability-core schedule) composes the digest and notification-core delivers it, with counts and links only for ZDR orgs. Avoid a second parallel ledger for notifications versus Space delivery.
dependencies: Provider and ZDR proof for any third-party sender
items.planeOwner: Application Plane
items.risks: Two ledgers diverging if not unified; email is a content-persisting boundary outside Verevon, so a ZDR org's digest must carry no bodies; digest fatigue without inactivity auto-pause.

alreadyPlanned.where: S4.4 durable Space completion delivery: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md (execution tracker, line 226); named gap delivery_ledger_not_built in apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:1618-1622

verevon.exactGap: notification-core has a leased delivery-attempt state machine (pending, claimed, sent_unconfirmed, acknowledged, failed, unknown), a lease-fenced worker and request-level idempotency keys, but the worker is off by default, needs NOTIFICATION_DELIVERY_MODE=novu plus a callback secret, has no bounded-retry or max-age policy, and rejects ZDR requests outright (service.go:296-301, delivery_worker.go:91-94). The Space delivery ledger is a named gap (delivery_ledger_not_built, spaces.rs:1618-1623) with no Space-event producers, and no per-user digest exists: insight-core's daily-brief scheduler (per-org/day idempotency key, email channel registered in migration 006) is deliberately disabled because an organisation is not a notification recipient.
reuse: notification-core delivery_attempts state machine, lease-fenced worker and callback verifier as the single ledger (do not build a parallel Space ledger)
notification-core request idempotency keys (FindByIdempotencyKey and resumeExisting) and insight-core BriefIdempotencyKey (daily_brief_<org>_<day>) as the digest dedupe pattern
insight-core briefs scheduler shape (round per tick, per-recipient key) and the channel-config registry rows for email (migrations 006 and 013)
Convex outbox lease pattern (spaceLifecycleEvents deliveryState, lease, nextAttemptAt) and ctx.scheduler.runAfter workers for a Space-side outbox or digest tick
notification-core identity_sync consumer pattern for event-fed user state
verevon.constraints: ZDR: notification-core refuses to enqueue ZDR requests today because the queue stores no payload and no transient-descriptor provider contract exists, so a ZDR org's counts-and-links digest cannot ride the existing queue; it needs an explicit content-free request class or retention mode ruled on by Control/ZDR policy, or the encrypted expiry-bound descriptor contract the code comment names. Email goes through Novu to an external provider, a content-persisting boundary whose provider and ZDR proof the S4.4 tracker still lists as open. Recipients must be real user subjects (the gateway may notify only the delegated user; an org id is not a recipient), and digest counts must come from Application-owned state (read markers, inbox feed) or owner-plane APIs and events, never DB reads, since pending approvals live in Model Plane. Digest links must resolve through normal Space membership checks (membership_changed revocations apply), so Space access never widens.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Treat finishing the S4.4 ledger (bounded retries, max-age, ZDR proof, durable feed reconciliation, HA) as the already-planned dependency rather than new work, and make the digest a separate Application Plane item: a per-user scheduler modelled on insight-core's briefs scheduler (using Convex scheduler or an outbox) that composes counts and links, instead of a capability-core Space schedule, because a digest is a projection and capability-core schedules fire Model runs needing Control fire decisions. Add the reply-to-source error path for agent runs as a Model-side change tracked separately. Gate any ZDR-org digest on the content-free request class decision.
verevon.effortNote: Kept at L, but note the split: the digest alone is M once the ledger and a content-free class exist; finishing the ledger is roadmapped S4.4 work and larger than the digest.
verevon.verdictReason: Status is partial and already planned (S4.4); the item understates what exists (idempotency keys, lease worker, email channel config, a disabled brief scheduler), overstates what ZDR allows (the queue rejects ZDR), and places digest composition in the wrong plane.

items.title: 'Catch me up' recap of what I missed, scoped to my own read access
items.summary: Add a 'Catch me up' entry point on the room header and the inbox. It runs a Model Plane recap turn over the unread messages and runs since the user's last read marker, prioritising items that mention the user or need action, with scopes unread, last 7 days or a custom range, and offers mark-as-read on completion. The scope is computed from the viewer's own access, ZDR is propagated, and the result is ephemeral for ZDR orgs.
items.whyItMatters: The highest-value AI feature for a returning user in an agent-heavy room: what did the agents do while I was away, and what needs me. Verevon owns its Model Plane and already puts agents in rooms, so this is an agent turn rather than a new subsystem, and it is the sort of attention feature Slack and Teams only bolt on.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Teams (cross-thread prioritised recap)
others: Slack (unread-only, last 7 days or custom range, plus a recurring-summary workflow step)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 sources; common
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Teams does a holistic, cross-thread recap prioritised by relevance, with read-aloud, and marks chats read when the recap is dismissed (REA). Slack offers unread-only, last-7-days and custom-range scopes and a workflow step for recurring summaries (DOC). Collect unread content since last_read for the requested scope (only content the viewer can access), summarise with a model, prioritise mentions and action items, offer mark-as-read.

verevonToday.gap: Only a 'Meeting Scribe' agent template that summarises the text conversation when it is mentioned. There is no 'catch me up' entry point, no unread-scoped or cross-room recap and no link to read markers.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: 'Catch me up' action in the room header and the inbox, registered in the action registry. Model Plane: a recap run invoked with the viewer's own read scope (never a wider room scope), zdr=true propagated, token and cost limits through the existing cost plane. Use the unread map and read markers from F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-02) to pick the window; optionally mark-as-read on completion. Output is not persisted for ZDR orgs.
dependencies: F-t1-009 (R-t1-05-02) read markers and unread map
Model Plane run with viewer-scoped access
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (recap run); Frontend Plane (entry point)
items.risks: Summaries quoting content the viewer cannot see if the scope is computed from the room rather than the viewer; cost on large rooms; stale recap if new messages arrive mid-run.

verevon.exactGap: The 'Catch me up' feature itself is absent: no catch-up action, recap run or unread-scoped summary exists in features/spaces or the gateway, and the only related thing is the Meeting Scribe agent template, which summarises the thread when mentioned and posts into the room for everyone. The substrate the item lists as a dependency is already shipped: an Application read marker per member per room (spaceReadMarkers.ts, spaces.mark_read action), an arrival-time snapshot and unread set (space-unread.ts, SpacePage.tsx), unread dots in the sidebar, and viewer-scoped transcript and work reads under Control read decisions (space_thread_transcript, space_work). The marker is a room-level timestamp over threads, not per message.

verevon.constraints: The recap must read only what the viewer may read: gather transcripts through the existing per-thread Control read decisions and the work projection, never a room-wide Model Plane scope, and bound the number of unread threads because decisions are per thread. The output is viewer-private, so it must not be posted into the room (a mention-driven Scribe reply is visible to every member); keep it ephemeral or store it in the viewer's personal Space. ZDR: a ZDR turn is a single stateless call, which fits an ephemeral recap; non-ZDR orgs need an explicit persistence choice. Application owns the read marker (timestamp only), Model Plane owns the recap call, Control owns the read decisions.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Put the entry points where the unread signal lives: the room header and the sidebar or Spaces list for cross-room recap, not the Inbox, which is the support ticket inbox with no Space unread state. Build it as a gateway-composed stateless summarize call (threads read under the viewer's Control decisions plus the run list since the arrival marker) instead of a new Model Plane run primitive with viewer-scoped multi-thread access, which does not exist, and avoid the room-agent persona path because it would post the answer to the room. Use the arrival snapshot, not the advancing durable marker, as the window start. The item's dependency on F-t1-009 read markers is already met at room level.
verevon.effortNote: M holds if the recap is stateless and gateway-composed; it becomes L if a persisted private result surface is added.
verevon.verdictReason: The feature is genuinely missing and cheap relative to its value, but the item misses that its read-marker dependency is shipped, points at the wrong inbox, and assumes a viewer-scoped Model Plane run primitive that does not exist; the stateless gateway-composed route is the buildable path.

items.title: Space UI quality baseline: locale-correct activity grammar and dates, server-held preferences, shared announcer, reduced motion, density and high contrast, failure screens
items.summary: Move the hard-coded Norwegian activity labels and forced nb-NO dates onto the i18n catalogue and the viewer locale (and pass the locale to the Model Plane); move locale and time zone into a layered, versioned user/org preference document next to the already server-side theme; promote the page-local live region into a shared, tick-keyed announcer with row narration and focus hand-off rules; audit Space animation for prefers-reduced-motion and add a density setting; add forced-colors/prefers-contrast rules for status marks and focus rings; and add a cannot-reach-Verevon page with start-up milestones.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon's Space accessibility and bilingual UI are already at or above buzz and QM; these small gaps (Norwegian-only activity grammar, no high-contrast rules, split preference storage) are where it would regress as the room grows.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (friendly activity vocabulary, announcer and pane focus rules); Teams (row narration, start-up milestones); Slack (cannot-connect page with log download); Buzz (reduced-motion gate, 3-level density); teams (63 locales with regional fallback map, app locale independent of the OS locale) for localization; slack (validated layered settings object with effective-value view) for preferences
others: grokbot (RTL, endonyms, zod-versioned settings that refuse bad files)
qm (palette import with contrast checks, density tiers)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-12-11] friendly copy 2 of 5 (Grok Bot, QM); accessibility 2 of 5 (Grok Bot, Teams); motion/density 2 of 5 (Buzz, Teams); shell failure UX 2 of 5 (Slack, Teams); differentiators [R-t1-11-06] Localization 3 of 5 (common); theming and high contrast 4 of 5 (table-stakes); preference store 3 of 5 (common).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-12-11] Catalog map from activity kind to localised friendly label. Announcer: two hidden regions (role=status, role=alert) each wrapping a span keyed by a counter so identical messages repeat, with announce(text, politeness). Pane navigation: outgoing pane inert and aria-hidden until animationend, then focus to the landing target once headings exist, skipped if focus is already elsewhere. Density: a data attribute scaling spacing variables; motion components check prefers-reduced-motion. Failure UX: milestone events (loaderStarted, firstPaint) to telemetry, critical load failure routes to an error page listing network checks and a "download logs" bundle. [R-t1-11-06] Message catalogs keyed by id with ICU plurals and a fallback chain; dir=rtl; Intl dates in the user locale. Preference schema with version and migrations; layers default < org policy < user < device; read API returns value plus source. Theme tokens as CSS variables with system, light, dark and contrast modes; org branding from config.

items.title: Room creation flows: templates with an agent roster and seed artifacts, clone, project and case Spaces bound to work objects, invite-on-mention
items.summary: Let a room be created from a declarative template (description, instructions, agent roster bound through the normal bind decision, seed canvas and list) or cloned from an existing room, in one transaction; enable project and case kinds with owner and roster, and have the Application Plane create a bound case or project Space when a ticket, customer case or project is created (membership from assignees, owner-plane ACLs stay authoritative, agent bindings still need human approval). When someone mentions a non-member or unbound agent, offer to add or bind them through the normal decisions.
items.whyItMatters: Buzz's templates with an agent roster are something neither Slack nor Teams has, and case Spaces are already planned in the Space authority ADR; together they turn recurring work into ready-made human-plus-agent rooms.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz (templates, non-member mention dialog); Buzz (SRC): a resource event lists coordinates and binds a channel, and the project signer gets no authority over member resources
others: qm (project rooms with source-tracked channel members)
Slack channel templates that pre-seed lists (DOC)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-02-11] templates 2 of 5 (buzz, teams; differentiator); project rooms 1 of 5 (qm); mention-to-invite 1 of 5 (buzz); unique to differentiator [R-t1-08-09] resource-bound rooms: 1 of 5, unique; templates: 1 of 5, unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-02-11] room_template(id, name, visibility, description, canvas_ref, agents[{definition_id, role, policy}]); instantiate creates the room then binds each agent through the normal decision. On send the server returns non_member_mentions[]; the client shows a dialog (safe action focused, invite withheld and explained when the actor cannot administer the room, draft restored on cancel); invite goes through the normal add-member decision. QM project store keeps channel-derived members separate so unlinking removes only them. [R-t1-08-09] Binding record {resource_ref, space_ref} created with the resource; a project is a list of resource refs plus a home space and only aggregates, since each resource's authorization still comes from its owner. A template is a declarative bundle {room settings, artifacts[], agents[]} instantiated in one transaction.

The only templates are three agent templates (Meeting Scribe, Status Agent, Knowledge Helper) in the create-agent dialog; no room template seeds artifacts.

External channel linking for projects stays with the future Channel Plane. Auto-archive the Space with the resource.

verevon.verdictReason: Status is partial (name-only rooms, three client-side agent presets, project and case kinds accepted by Control but refused by the gateway); the approach needs a saga framing, a registry placement and a split, and the case-Space half depends on undefined ADR semantics.

items.title: Governed Space skills and plugin bundles (ecosystem-compatible manifests)
items.summary: Give skills a Space scope and a review lifecycle (draft, reviewed, published, archived, with review invalidated by any edit and signed manifests), and let the org plugin registry accept Claude-style and Cursor-style marketplace manifests with git-sha pinning and a variables schema, fanning components out to the skill store, MCP registry and hook runner. A Space manager can then enable an org-activated plugin or publish a room skill, never beyond what the org allows.
items.whyItMatters: A team can curate room-specific know-how ('how we run incident review') safely, which is how agents get better in a shared room, and reading existing plugin ecosystems gives Verevon agents many capabilities for little effort. It extends two existing assets (the / skill picker and the admin-activated plugin packs).

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Governed skills: 2 of 5 (differentiator); plugin bundles: 2 of 5 (differentiator)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: qm's SkillStore runs draft->reviewed->published->archived with HMAC-signed manifests verified on resolve, visibleFor(principal, scope) filtering, supporting files materialised only for speakers who can see the skill, and git skill packs pinned to a ref with visible ineligibility reasons. Grok Bot reads both .cursor-plugin and .claude-plugin marketplace.json, pins git sources to a 40-hex sha, declares a variables JSON-schema (writeOnly marks secrets) and registers each component (commands, agents, skills, rules, hooks, mcpServers) with its subsystem; buzz persona packs are a simpler variant.

verevonToday.gap: Skills exist with org and personal scope (badges) and are resolved server-side in Model Gateway from structured skill_ids; Settings has an org plugin-pack section where an admin registers a JSON manifest (tools, skills, hooks) that stays inactive until activated (spot-check). Missing: Space-scoped skills, a review/publish lifecycle, signed manifests, git pack import, Space-level plugin enablement, ecosystem manifest compatibility, sha pinning and a variables schema. Governed Space skills are plan item S3.5.

items.approach: Model Plane skill store: add scope=space and the review state machine (promotion persists immutable reviewed versions and scoped activation in the database, per S3.5), signed manifests and progressive disclosure; Control Plane decides who may publish to a scope (editor and above for a Space). Plugin registry: accept .claude-plugin and .cursor-plugin manifests with sha pinning and a variables schema, keeping admin activation inactive by default; components fan out to the skill store, the MCP registry (F-t1-037 (R-t1-06-02)) and the hook runner. Optional git pack importer in Ingestion Plane: HTTPS only, DNS pinning and private-address denial, bounded files, symlink and binary rejection (S3.5 slice 4). Space cockpit enables an org-activated plugin per room.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (skill store, plugin registry); Control Plane (publish decisions); Ingestion Plane (git pack import)
items.risks: Skill-borne prompt injection (the review gate must cover the exact body); plugin hooks run code, so require sha pins and admin activation; supply-chain risk of third-party manifests.

items.title: Agents attend Zoom, Meet and Teams meetings as visible guests through an Ingestion capture worker, with approval-gated chat drafts
items.summary: Let a user hand an agent a meeting link, or let it pick one up from the user calendar. A capture worker joins as a clearly labelled guest after per-meeting or standing consent, feeds the transcript into the F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-02) pipeline, and leaves. The agent may post to the meeting chat only through drafts that a human approves, with an internal-meeting mark respected. Start after F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-02) and F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-03); it does not depend on F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01).
items.whyItMatters: Gives Verevon meeting coverage on day one for customers who live in Teams, Zoom or Meet, without building a conferencing stack, and it feeds Space knowledge. It follows the rule that the Model proposes and Quarry executes: the bot is an Ingestion capture worker and the agent only proposes chat posts.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (SRC, medium confidence from RPC names and strings)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5 (Grok Bot only); unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Tools JoinMeeting(link), LeaveMeeting, ListMeetings, ReadMeetingTranscript, RespondInMeeting; a server-side bot joins as a guest named after the agent; chat posts go through a MeetingChatDraft {meeting_id, body, mark_internal} that a human approves; per-meeting or blanket consent card; versioned summaries per meeting; admin setting for who can see meeting records; meetings addressed as meeting:{id} like other channels.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane: a meeting-capture worker (headless browser guest through Quarry, or a vendor meeting-bot API) authorised through integration-corev2 and Quarry browser grants; Quarry executes or rejects the join and any chat post. Transcript or audio goes to the F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-02) pipeline and Data Plane. Model Plane: Space agent tools ListMeetings, ReadMeetingTranscript, DraftMeetingChat that only propose. Space UI: consent card and approval card for chat drafts, meeting-link intake in the Meetings section, link discovery from calendar.events. Consent and internal mark enforced by the F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-03) policy; standing consent stored in Control, not in the browser.

verevon.constraints: Channel Plane is docs-only and S5.1 leaves its runtime status open, so capture ownership needs an ADR before code. Model proposes, Quarry executes applies to Model-proposed browser actions; a deterministic join bot is not one, so do not describe the join as a Quarry accept/reject decision. Prefer a vendor meeting-bot API or the platforms' own transcript/recording export through integration-corev2 connectors under the user's delegated consent as the first adapter, and treat a Quarry headless-browser guest as a research spike only. Remove the claim that Quarry executes or rejects the join; keep Quarry for Model-proposed browser steps. Chat drafts should reuse the approval and attestation path rather than a new draft object.
verevon.effortNote: L only if a vendor bot API or platform export is used; becomes XL if a Quarry headless guest with audio capture is built. Both are gated by F-t1-050 and an ownership ADR.
verevon.verdictReason: Correctly described as absent, but it depends on F-t1-050 (which itself lacks a shared-room authority path), on an unresolved Channel versus Ingestion ownership decision and on external ToS and consent risk. It belongs after the upload-based meeting MVP.

items.title: Duplex voice for agents: a voice front that delegates to the Space agent, then agents as attributed participants in room calls
items.summary: Phase A (M, no SFU needed): inside a Space, a user holds a realtime voice conversation with an agent. A fast voice persona talks and its only tools delegate: send_task hands real work to the existing agent run in the Space (still behind approval gates) and a history search covers Space threads and past voice sessions; each agent gets voice, speed and language settings. Phase B (L, after F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01)): a server-side participant per invited agent hears the call through STT, answers with an attributed audio track, and stops when a human starts talking.
items.whyItMatters: This is the defining hybrid moment of the Space vision: humans and agents in the same voice room, and a personal agent that can be tasked hands-free. The front and worker split avoids a second agent brain, and doing it server-side is better than Buzz, whose agent voice runs on the owner desktop.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (SRC) for the voice-front and worker split; Buzz (SRC) for agents as audio participants with floor control
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5 each (Grok Bot, Buzz); unique.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grok Bot: realtime session (session.update, input_audio_buffer.append, response.create/cancel) with voice tools send_task(constraints), recall_text_messages and search_conversations{query, scope this-chat|earlier|everything, from, to, if_missing}; worker results come back as async updates the persona announces; one active voice chat per user and ending needs confirmation; the refusal text for send_task tells the model not to drop prohibitions or approval requirements; per-agent voice_id, voice_speed, voice_language. Buzz: agent audio publisher authenticates as the agent and shows in the roster; VAD with about 300 ms silence flush; any human speech cancels agent TTS (barge-in); agent speaks only when addressed.

evidence: apps/Model Plane/rust/services/model-gateway/src/http_routes.rs:448-450 and :4900-4945 (SRC: /v1/ai/realtime/session creates a realtime session returning client secret and websocket URL, default server_vad turn detection, ZDR-gated through decide_content_route)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/voice/VoiceModeDialog.tsx and voice-mode-state.ts:1-35 (SRC: tap-to-talk dictation, review, send, optional read-aloud)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/DashboardComposer.tsx:3683 (SRC: VoiceModeDialog mounted only in the dashboard composer, not in Spaces)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/api/speech-client.ts:6,91 (SRC: governed TTS pinned to azure-speech, fails closed on a different provider)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:402-420 (SRC: room posts go through streamChat with spaceRef and mentionedAgentRef)
verevonToday.gap: A realtime session route and a tested half-duplex voice mode exist, but nothing is full-duplex, Space-scoped or delegating to a Space agent, there is no per-agent voice profile and no agent audio identity in a room. The baseline also records that personal agents are not possible today (a personal Space cannot hold an agent), which limits a personal-agent voice phase until that is changed.

items.approach: Model Plane: a realtime voice session type whose only tools are send_task (calls the existing agent run API in the Space so approval gates and Control decisions still apply) and search_conversations (Space threads read under the read decision); add voice_id, voice_speed and voice_language to the agent profile in the registry behind SpaceCreateAgentDialog. Frontend: upgrade VoiceModeDialog into a duplex call island that can mount in SpaceRoomComposer and reuse the call store from F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01). Phase B: a Model Plane SFU participant per invited agent subscribing to room audio, streaming to /v1/ai/realtime, publishing an agent track under the agent identity, label shown in the roster; floor policy cancels agent playback on any human speech (response.cancel) and the agent speaks only when explicitly invited to the call or addressed, consistent with the explicit-invocation rule. Enforce F-t1-050 (R-t1-03-03) before the agent hears the room.
dependencies: Agent run API and approval gates
Agents in personal Spaces (agents-in-the-room category) for personal-agent voice
items.planeOwner: Model Plane
items.risks: ZDR attestation for realtime providers (the route already fails closed). Cost per minute. Agents talking over humans; always label agent voices. Delegated actions must still hit in-room approval gates and must carry the constraints of the spoken request.

verevon.exactGap: Model Plane already exposes POST /v1/ai/realtime/session (inference-core create_realtime_session returns a provider client secret and websocket URL, server_vad by default, ZDR fail-closed through decide_content_route and reject_unattested_zdr_modality), but the BFF has no route for it, no frontend caller exists, and the session request has no tools field, so nothing is duplex or can delegate to a Space agent. The shipped voice mode is half-duplex (VoiceModeDialog: tap, record up to 60 s, governed dictate route, review, send, optional Azure TTS read-aloud) and is mounted only in DashboardComposer, not in Spaces; there is no per-agent voice profile, a personal Space cannot hold an agent (docs, 2026-09-07), and no call substrate (SFU, WebRTC) exists in the frontend, gateway, Model Plane, Application Plane or Ingestion Plane.

apps/Model Plane/proto/model_plane/v1/inference.proto:1156-1175 (CreateRealtimeSessionRequest fields: model, provider_hint, voice, instructions, formats, turn detection)

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:402 (room posts go through streamChat with spaceRef)
