apps/Model Plane/docs/MODEL_PLANE_V2_PARITY.md:31 (realtime partial; browser/WebRTC client integration missing)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/space-defenition.md:150-160,386 (invocation rule; personal Space cannot hold an agent as of 2026-09-07)

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains (grep: no realtime route); src, gateway, Model Plane, Application Plane, Quarry crates, integration-corev2 (grep: no livekit, mediasoup or RTCPeerConnection)
reuse: model-gateway /v1/ai/realtime and the inference-core RealtimeProvider (client-secret broker, ZDR gate)
VoiceModeDialog, voice-mode-state machine and voice-recorder mic handling
governed TTS chain (speech-client.ts, gateway ai.rs, inference-core) for read-aloud and agent voice names
SpaceRoomComposer streamChat path so delegated work keeps the Control append decision, approvals and attribution
Space agent bindings and registry profile for per-agent voice fields
verevon.constraints: A realtime session hands the browser a client secret and a direct provider socket, so the Model Plane cannot meter cost, enforce tools server-side or see the audio; tool calls must be executed by the browser through the normal BFF Space send and approval path, and the Space context has to be pinned in the session instructions at mint time. ZDR voice is refused today, so ZDR Spaces get no duplex voice. History search needs a Space read decision. Agents speak only when invited (invocation rule), which matches the item. Phase B needs a server-side call participant and a call substrate that does not exist (F-t1-029).
verevon.approachAdjustment: Add a BFF route that mints a realtime session with Space-scoped instructions and a tool schema (requires a tools field on CreateRealtimeSessionRequest), keep send_task and search execution in the browser via the existing composer and read routes, and treat per-minute cost as unmetered until a Model-side relay exists. Do not describe the Model Plane as running the voice tools. Keep Phase B as a separate, later item behind the call substrate.
verevon.effortNote: Phase A is L, not M: BFF route, proto change, a duplex WebRTC or WebSocket client with echo control and barge-in, send_task bridge and per-agent voice fields. Phase B is XL and blocked on a call substrate.
verevon.verdictReason: The Model Plane half exists and the half-duplex mode is shipped, so the item is right that duplex is missing, but Phase A understates the work and mislocates tool execution. Phase B should be demoted until a call layer is decided.

items.title: Screen sharing in calls with a sharing indicator, sensitive-surface redaction, and the same cue for agents acting in a room
items.summary: Publish a getDisplayMedia track to the call as a second SFU track, show a persistent "you are sharing" bar with Stop, and switch the app into a redacted mode while sharing so approval cards, secrets and token-like fields are masked (a web page cannot exclude its own windows from capture). Reuse the border and indicator design for the agent run live view and the Quarry browser view so humans see when an agent is acting.
items.whyItMatters: Screen share is the main reason people start work calls, and it is cheap once an SFU exists. The agent-acting cue gives one consistent trust signal for the Model proposes, Quarry executes browser model, where the baseline shows agent work is opaque inside the room.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (SRC): a native border overlay follows the shared window and the picker excludes the app own sensitive windows
others: Teams (SRC): deeper capture pipeline, annotation and single-controller remote control
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 2 of 5 (Slack, Teams); common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Picker with thumbnails clamped to 480 px that filters excluded windows; an overlay with border width and colour that tracks the window bounds; share published as its own track. Web equivalent: navigator.mediaDevices.getDisplayMedia, an in-app sharing bar, and a redact-sensitive-surfaces mode.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/DashboardComposer.tsx:1915-1950 (SRC: addScreenshotFile uses getDisplayMedia for a single frame, not a stream)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/remote_support.rs:1-12 (SRC: RustDesk config only; sessions run browser to hbbs/hbbr and bypass the gateway, no durable record)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/dashboard/home/BrowserChrome.tsx:497,559-560 (SRC: browser control mode with human_takeover)
verevonToday.gap: No human screen share in Spaces. Adjacent pieces only: a one-frame screenshot capture in the dashboard composer, RustDesk remote-support config that is not a Space feature and leaves no audit record, and agent live-view and human-takeover controls that are not reachable from a Space.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: after F-t1-029 (R-t1-03-01), add getDisplayMedia publishing to the call store with a sharing state; a sharing banner; a global redact mode that masks SpaceApprovalPanel content, secrets and credential-like inputs while sharing; extract the border and indicator component and mount it on the agent run live view and, once Space-scoped browser runs exist, on the Quarry browser view in the room. No annotation or remote control in the first cut. Keep RustDesk remote support separate and add a durable session record there later if it is ever surfaced in Spaces.
dependencies: Space-scoped agent browser view (agents-in-the-room category) for the agent cue
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Leaking approval cards or secrets during a share, since the web cannot exclude its own windows. Browser support for display capture constraints varies.

verevon.exactGap: No call, huddle or live screen-share code exists in Spaces or anywhere under apps/ (git grep finds no RTCPeerConnection, SFU, livekit or mediasoup use; getDisplayMedia appears once, as a one-frame screenshot capture in DashboardComposer.tsx:1915-1950), so this item cannot start before the call stack it depends on (F-t1-029), which is also absent. The agent-acting cue is only partly present as an 'is working...' row per post and a composer line (SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:349-366, SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:176-182, 617-630); there is no Space browser view, the FleetRunConsole live-view cells are placeholder text (FleetRunConsole.tsx:116-131), and the real hosted-browser view with human_takeover lives only on Home/chat (BrowserChrome.tsx:497). The Space definition lists huddles as an explicit non-goal (space-defenition.md:352-353).
reuse: DashboardComposer.addScreenshotFile getDisplayMedia handling (stop all tracks, cancel is a no-op) as the capture starting point
Space working row and composer line plus space-live-work.ts live-run projection as the agent-acting cue that already exists in text form
BrowserChrome controlMode/human_takeover chip and approval bubble as the design source for an agent-acting border once a Space browser view exists
SpaceApprovalPanel as the surface to mask in a redacted-while-sharing mode
packages/remote-core (RustDesk WebSocket client used by RemoteSupportPage) is a separate remote-desktop path and not a base for an SFU share
verevon.constraints: No plane owns a media/SFU service today, so human screen share is not a Frontend-only change: a call needs a media service (Application Plane realtime or Infra) with join authorization from a Control Space-membership decision, and ZDR requires that no recording, transcript or content is retained. The agent-acting cue must be rendered from Model Plane run state and, for browsers, Quarry session state; the Frontend only displays it (Model proposes, Quarry executes), and a Space-scoped agent browser view does not exist yet. A web page cannot exclude its own windows from capture, so in-app redaction is best-effort and must not be advertised as a guarantee. Calls/huddles conflict with the documented Space non-goal, so this needs a product decision.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split the item. Keep the agent-acting cue as its own small item built on the existing run-status projection (S, Frontend only, extends the 'is working' row with the current tool or browser step). Move human screen share behind an explicit call decision as an optional later item and drop the claim that it is cheap, since the SFU and signalling do not exist. If it is ever built, scope the first cut to share-a-tab with a sharing bar and a warning, and treat redaction of approval cards as a UI nicety rather than a safeguard.
verevon.effortNote: M holds only for the incremental share track after a call stack exists; none exists, and an SFU plus authorization and signalling is an XL by itself. The agent-cue half alone is S.
verevon.verdictReason: Absent, hard-dependent on a call stack that also does not exist, and contrary to the documented Space non-goal on huddles; only the agent-acting cue half deserves to stay as a small separate item.

items.title: Search operators with Verevon-native filters, typed result tabs and recent-search history
items.summary: Port buzz's operator parser (from:, in:, with:, is:, has:, before:/after:/on:, quoted phrases, exclusion, trailing *) as a pure TS module, add Verevon-specific operators (agent:, has:approval, has:run, has:artifact, is:thread), and render results in tabs (threads, agents, runs, approvals, artifacts, documents) with counts. The gateway fans out to owner-plane APIs in parallel and returns {hits, counts, failed[], limited[]}; recent searches stay in browser storage per viewer.
items.whyItMatters: Power users and agents (which can emit structured filters directly) get precise recall, and one search covers Verevon objects that Slack and Teams do not have. Agent- and run-aware operators would be a differentiator no reference has. The failed[]/limited[] contract keeps an empty result distinguishable from a gap.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: slack (grammar, DOC) with buzz parser (SRC) and teams result domains (REA)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: operators 3 of 5 (table-stakes); result domains 3 of 5 (common)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: buzz parseSearchOperators splits on whitespace, recognises an operator only at token start, leaves malformed values (e.g. invalid dates) in the free text, resolves names to ids at the call site and converts dates to since/until with an exclusive "before"; filters {authors[], spaces[], since, until, is[], has[]} go to the server as SQL predicates before ranking. Teams fans one query out to per-domain resolvers (messages, files by type, meetings, people, channels, settings), returns hit types and per-domain counts, and renders tabs with type-specific facets and date presets. qm SearchBackend registry returns failed[] and limited[] arrays.

verevonToday.gap: No message search, so no operators, tabs, filters or history. The Knowledge tab lists documents and wiki read-only without search or filters, though it already reports per-section gaps. Verevon-native objects (threads, agents, runs, approvals, artifacts) are not searchable.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: pure TS parser module plus Solid search view with tabs; name resolution against the Space roster and org members. Share the filter struct with the agent history tool (F-t1-038 (R-t1-04-03)) so humans and agents use one grammar. Gateway BFF composes per-domain calls to owner planes (Session Core messages, Data Plane documents, Application Plane activity/run projections) in parallel with a per-backend timeout, each with its own Control decision, no cross-plane DB join. Keep search history in browser storage first, since server-side query history may be forbidden under ZDR.
dependencies: Owner-plane search endpoints for runs, approvals and artifacts (not confirmed to exist)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (parser, UI, gateway fan-out); owner planes expose per-domain search
items.risks: Name resolution must not reveal people the viewer cannot see; date timezone ambiguity; gateway fan-out must not drift into a cross-plane DB join; slowest backend sets latency; scores from different backends are not comparable.

verevon.exactGap: No search over Space messages, threads, runs, approvals or artifacts exists: gateway search routes cover only web, similar, suggest, images, videos and answer (search.rs:39-45), the Cmd/Ctrl+K overlay is knowledge retrieval plus a client-side title filter over local chat history (navbar.rs:262-283, CoreNavbar.tsx:403-409), and the Space Knowledge tab is a read-only list with no search box (SpaceKnowledgePanel.tsx:82-110). Session Core has no search RPC, and the retrieval engine strips ':' field selectors from queries (textquery.rs:127), so an operator grammar has nothing to compile to until a Session Core message search (F-t1-018) exists. The one existing pattern to copy is the ZDR-gated, identity-keyed browser history for web searches (web-history.ts:1-40).
evidence: buzz: desktop/src/features/search/lib/parseSearchOperators.test.mjs (parser to port; confirmed present via git grep)
reuse: buzz parseSearchOperators as the pure TS parser to port (ships with tests)

Session Core message columns that operators can map onto: author_subject_id (from:), agent_name (agent:), thread/space id (in:), created_at (before/after), per-message audience columns (migration 0025)
The Space activity route (GET /spaces/:ref/activity) which already composes threads, runs, approvals, receipts and grants, so run and approval tabs can start as a filter over that per-room projection
web-history.ts pattern (ZDR gate via chat-retention, identity-keyed storage, URL validation) for recent searches
The F-t1-018 search UI shell and the CoreNavbar overlay
verevon.constraints: Message search must be a Session Core (Model Plane) read under the same Control shared-read decision and audience filtering as the transcript; the gateway may fan out and compose but must not join across planes, and each backend needs its own Control decision. Name-to-id resolution for from: must come from the Space roster the viewer is already allowed to read. ZDR threads are temporary and must stay unsearchable, and recent-search history must stay browser-local and obey isLocalRetentionAllowed. Do not forward operator text to retrieval-engine/Quickwit, which strips ':' syntax; parse in the client or gateway and send structured filters.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Sequence it behind F-t1-018. The operator parser is an S module that can land with the search UI, mapping to a structured filter {authors, spaces, since, until, is, has, agent}. Typed tabs for runs, approvals and artifacts should first be a client-side filter over the per-room activity projection (no new owner-plane endpoint), with cross-room fan-out only later; the item's 'owner-plane search endpoints not confirmed to exist' dependency is true for Session Core messages but not for per-room runs and approvals. Share the filter struct with the agent history tool (F-t1-038) as proposed.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for this item alone; it excludes the Session Core message search (F-t1-018), which is a separate M to L Model Plane build and the real critical path.
verevon.verdictReason: Nothing exists and the item is blocked on message search that does not exist; operators are a refinement of search, not a first-order Space need, so it should follow F-t1-018 rather than lead.

items.title: Room header and pulse rail extras: live counts, pinned posts first, user-pinned resource tabs and a budget meter; PWA share target and MCP apps later
items.summary: Keep the six cockpit tabs as default, add header counts (open approvals, running work, documents) from existing projections, show pinned posts first, and allow user-pinnable extra tabs (link, document, later canvas) stored as Space metadata with view-only grants controlling access. Add a usage meter once per-Space cost attribution and non-zero token counts exist. Later add a PWA share target so a file or text can be sent to a room agent from anywhere, and render MCP UI resources in a sandboxed iframe whose tool calls go through the Model Gateway authority path.
items.whyItMatters: QM's scope page and Slack's tabs make a room's resources one click away; useful polish once canvas, cost and PWA exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (scope-centred page and top-bar tool buttons with 60 s cached counts); Slack for user-added tabs and bookmarks; Grok Bot for the usage meter; teams
others: Slack (Pins tab auto-created on first pin, bookmark folders)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-12-09] header shelf 2 of 5 (Slack, QM; differentiator); usage meter 1 of 5 (Grok Bot; unique) [R-t1-06-12] Each capability appears in 1 of 5 sources (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-12-09] Scope model {personal|project|channel|group} drives contextMeta(scope) panels with manage actions; the top bar shows breadcrumb plus tool buttons whose counts are cached per scope for 60 s, and opening a tool keeps the session scope. Slack lists tabs per conversation with "show by default". Grok Bot: usage policy {thresholds:[75,90]} feeding a meter component and a limit-hit state with upgrade or credit options. [R-t1-06-12] Teams stores a tab as (app id, content URL, entity id, scope) on the conversation and renders it in an iframe with per-viewer access checks; its package registers protocols and a share target, and share-from-web carries a compose note and verifies the active account. Grok Bot renders MCP app resources in a sandboxed frame whose tool calls pass a host bridge and the normal permission checks (feature-gated).

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceCockpit.tsx:61-110 and components/SpacePage.tsx:408-486 (six fixed tabs, no counts)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:4890-4925 (space_actions echoes the org catalog only)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceRoomComposer.tsx:541-567 and lib/activity-grammar.ts:694-730 (budget_exceeded rendered as a refusal linking to the spend ceiling)
verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-12-09] No user-added tabs or bookmarks, no counts in the header, pins not shown first, no room-level view of skills, connectors or memory (S3.x), and no proactive meter or per-room spend (token counts are 0 from Session Core, so a meter would mislead). [R-t1-06-12] The cockpit has six fixed tabs (Chat, Work, Knowledge, Activity, Agent, Members) and no pinned or custom tabs. There is no share target or protocol handler and no native shell. No MCP UI resource handling was found in model-gateway (a grep for ui:// and MCP app terms returned nothing this pass), but the MCP app renderer status in the Frontend was not checked.

items.approach: [R-t1-12-09] Frontend Plane: header counts from existing Work, Activity and Knowledge projections, with unknown rendered as unknown; a user-pinnable tab type stored as Space metadata in Application Plane (link and document first, canvas after category 08); pinned posts first. The meter is last: Model Plane cost service publishes per-org and per-Space usage summaries and Session Core must return real token counts before the pulse rail shows a meter. [R-t1-06-12] Frontend Plane: allow pinning Knowledge documents and vetted internal links as extra cockpit tabs, restricting embeds to internal resources first (clickjacking). Add a PWA share target and deep links building on the existing in-app deep links (baseline v-space-ui-043). MCP apps after F-t1-026 (R-t1-06-04): sandboxed iframe with a postMessage bridge that forwards tool calls only through the Model Gateway authority path.
dependencies: Per-Space cost attribution in Model Plane and non-zero token counts from Session Core (meter only)
F-t1-037 (R-t1-06-02) Space tool cockpit (for MCP apps)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (meter data from Model Plane)
items.risks: [R-t1-12-09] Tab sprawl; counts and meter must show unknown, never zero, when a projection is unavailable; the meter must not expose another member's spend. [R-t1-06-12] Arbitrary-site embedding (clickjacking); sandbox escape and data exfiltration from MCP app frames; share-target account mismatch.

alreadyPlanned.where: [R-t1-12-09] apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/SPACE_PAGE_AUDIT_2026-09-06.md section 17 (The later tier, about lines 1595-1625) records per-room spend as blocked, and S3.x covers room skills/connectors/memory panels (about lines 253-257).

verevon.exactGap: Pin state is half shipped: Session Core already lists pinned threads first (session-core grpc.rs:5590) and the room renders a Pinned flag and an author-only Pin/Unpin control, but SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:137 re-sorts every post by updated_at, so pinned posts are marked rather than first. gateway shares.rs plus user-core resource_grants (view-only) for pinned document tabs
ChatArtifactPanel sandboxed srcdoc iframe pattern (sandbox allow-scripts, no same-origin) for any later MCP UI frame
cost_entries.metadata jsonb as a place to tag Space if per-Space attribution is added
verevon.constraints: Tab and pinned-tab metadata belong in Application Plane (spaces table), while document access stays decided per viewer by Control resource grants so a pinned tab never widens an owner-plane ACL or leaks a title to a viewer without a grant. Embeds are limited by the nginx CSP (frame-src only Cloudflare and DIBS, frame-ancestors none), so link tabs should be link-outs or internal routes first. Per-Space spend needs cost-core or Model Plane attribution first (Control owns pricing, the browser must not multiply tokens), counts must show unknown rather than zero when a projection is unavailable, and MCP apps are blocked behind governed MCP execution because model-gateway denies mcp__ tools inline until capability-core provides a durable binding.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split the item. Ship now: pinned-first (sort pinned before the chronological tail or render a Pinned strip above the timeline) and header counts lifted from the Work and approval projections, with unknown shown as unknown. Next: user-pinned tabs limited to internal routes and Knowledge documents, stored as Space metadata in Application Plane. Keep the meter, PWA share target and MCP apps as separate later items; the meter needs Space attribution in cost-core, real token counts from Session Core and a corrected spend-ceiling semantic (the ceiling is compared to a lifetime aggregate per the Space page audit), otherwise it would mislead.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the near-term subset (pinned-first S, counts S to M, internal pinned tabs M); the meter, PWA share target and MCP apps are each L or XL and should be tracked separately.
verevon.verdictReason: Pinned-first is a client sort defect rather than missing infrastructure and counts partly exist in SpacePulse, while the meter, PWA and MCP parts are blocked on other work, so the item should be split and the first two promoted to quick wins.

items.title: Shareable, versioned agent templates with an export policy, and an internal catalogue of org agents and skills
items.summary: Replace the three hard-coded agent templates with user-published templates (immutable versions, active-version pointer, org or team visibility, share link, an export policy that never copies credentials, memory or grants; import re-runs roster confirmation), and build an internal 'agents in this org' catalogue as a read model over the agent registry with admin approval before listing. Defer public third-party marketplace listings.
items.whyItMatters: Grok Bot shows templates and a catalogue make good agents spread inside an org; it matters after personal agents exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-06-09] 2 of 5 sources; differentiator [R-t1-04-11] 1 of 5 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-06-09] Grok Bot templates have CRUD with visibility (PUBLIC|TEAM), an active version, an export policy, chat-link import and creator attribution; a template record {share_id, active_version, visibility, owner_type, blob_object_key} points at immutable version blobs, and the export policy strips secrets, memory and connections. Buzz persona packs and snapshots are a file-based variant. [R-t1-04-11] Listing objects with a status workflow (PENDING_REVIEW, LISTED, DELISTED) and a review queue, plugin lifecycle states, a browse API with category, featured and sort, per-team popularity counts, and install creating an org-scoped installation subject to admin policy. Slack and Teams app directories are INF only (not evidenced in this category).

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-06-09] Agent creation offers three hard-coded templates; there are no user-published templates, versions, share links or export policy. Personal per-user agents are absent (baseline v-space-backend-070: Control refuses personal membership replacement), so the 'copy a colleague's personal agent' flow needs that first. Whether Application Plane agent definitions are versioned was not verified. [R-t1-04-11] No marketplace or app directory for Spaces. The org-wide agent registry answers presence, not discovery of new agents, and MCP/plugins are configured org-wide in Settings only.

items.approach: [R-t1-06-09] Application Plane: agent definitions gain immutable versions and a template record (visibility, active version, share id). Control Plane governs visibility (org or team) and the export policy, which never copies credentials, memory, grants or connector references. Import re-runs roster confirmation and binding policy. Frontend: publish and import actions in the Create Agent dialog and the Agent tab. [R-t1-04-11] Start internal: a read model over existing agent definitions and skills with listing status and admin approval (Control Plane owns policy, Application Plane projects the list), browse route in the gateway, directory tab in the Frontend. Defer third-party listings until plugin/MCP governance exists.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (definitions, versions, catalogue read model) with Control Plane (visibility, export policy)
items.risks: [R-t1-06-09] Leaking instructions or connector references through a template; imported templates carrying prompt-injection payloads; import must not inherit the author's grants. [R-t1-04-11] Third-party plugins bypassing ZDR or the rule that the Model proposes and Quarry executes browser actions.

verevon.exactGap: Agent creation offers three hard-coded client-side templates that only copy text into the form (SpaceCreateAgentDialog AGENT_TEMPLATES); there are no user-published templates, immutable versions, share links or export policy, and the Convex agents table has no version field. The internal catalogue half is partly shipped: an org-wide agent registry (/api/v1/agents/installations, ADR-0002) and a per-room installable-agents list with bind-existing (listInstallableSpaceAgentsForGateway, bindExistingSpaceAgentForGateway) already let a room pick any org agent, but with no listing status, approval, skills or browse metadata. Agents are org-owned records (orgId, optional createdBy) that also hold embed publicSecret and tool/knowledge references, so sharing a definition directly would leak fields.

apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/spaceAgents.ts:486-515,529-560 (listInstallableSpaceAgentsForGateway; bindExistingSpaceAgentForGateway born pending, room-only, mention-only, no tools, never inherits Studio config)

apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:686-700,3165-3200 (installations and available routes; registry answers presence, not authority)
apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/repository.go:655-690 (personal Space membership cannot be replaced)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/agents/lib/verevon-agent-blueprints.tsx:774 (second static blueprint array for the Agents surface)
reuse: listInstallableSpaceAgentsForGateway and the org agent registry as the catalogue read model (add listing status and approval)
bindExistingSpaceAgentForGateway born-with policy (pending, room-only, mention-only, no tools) as the import behaviour
SpaceCreateAgentDialog template list as the seed for system templates
MCP server share route as the sharing-model precedent
Control roster confirmation for imported agents
verevon.constraints: Application Plane (Convex) owns agent definitions, so templates and versions belong there; Control only decides roster/role and any team-level visibility. The registry answers presence, not authority, so the catalogue must not imply that a listed agent can be invoked in a room. Export must be an explicit field allowlist: never copy publicSecret or embed config, connector or knowledge references, grants, memory or binding policy. Import must re-run Control roster confirmation and start with the restrictive binding defaults (pending, no tools), never inheriting the author's grants. Public third-party listings stay out of scope until plugin/MCP governance exists.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Shrink the catalogue half to an incremental extension of the existing installable-agents read model (listing status, admin approval, include skills) rather than a new read model. Build templates as a new Convex agentTemplates table with immutable version rows, an active-version pointer, org visibility, and a field-allowlist export; import creates a normal definition plus pending binding. Remove the dependency on personal agents: org-visible templates do not need them, and 'copy a colleague's agent' is a later add-on.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: templates and versioning are M; the catalogue extension is S because the read model and bind flow already exist.
verevon.verdictReason: Templates, versions and export policy are absent, but the org agent registry and installable-agents bind flow already deliver most of the internal catalogue, and the personal-agent dependency is unnecessary for org templates, so the item should be reduced to templates plus an allowlist export and an incremental catalogue extension.

items.title: Scoped agent context and promotion path: team layer, setup manifests, publish to team, service accounts
items.summary: Extend ResolvedSpaceContext with a team layer (included only when the actor is on the team and the room is configured for it), add explicit scope-to-scope grants that stay with the resource-owning plane, and add scoped setup manifests (org, team, user) for agent computers. Once personal agents exist, add a publish-to-team flow with a step-by-step carry-over proposal (never secrets) and agent-owned service credentials scoped per binding.
items.whyItMatters: Verevon already has the stricter half (decisions bound to audience and owner-plane ACL, authored instruction hierarchy). The missing half is how agents and their computers are configured at team level and promoted from a person's own agent to a team's, which GrokBot's vision of personal agents needs.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: qm (scope layering), grokbot (publish, manifests, service accounts)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: each 1 of 5 (qm or grokbot only); unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM resolve(actor, scope, audience) mounts org (read-only), each applicable team (read-only) and the active scope (read-write) and composes instructions, policies and granted handles; handlesForAudience returns only what every participant is entitled to. GrokBot: PublishToTeam builds a carry-over proposal (skills, plugins, memories, automations) the owner confirms item by item and never copies personal chats; setup_manifest(scope_kind USER|TEAM|ORGANIZATION) merged org, then team, then user at sandbox creation; team agents act through service-account credentials.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:3720-3888 and :4231-4398 (authored instruction hierarchy: platform, org, Space, user persona, agent persona)
apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/repository.go:670-673 (personal Space membership immutable, so no personal agents)
no setup-manifest code found by name search in the Model Plane (comparator check)
verevonToday.gap: No team layer, no cross-scope grants, no setup manifests (status unknown), no publish flow because personal agents cannot exist yet, and provider-level agent service accounts are unverified.

items.approach: Phase A (after teams): add a team layer to ResolvedSpaceContext; resource grants live with the owner plane (Data Plane for files, Model Plane for skills) and are referenced by Control, never in a central table. Phase B (Model Plane sandboxes): setup manifests per org, then team and user, restricted to an allowlisted package registry. Phase C (after personal agents and agent access list): publish-to-team in the Model Plane with a Control publish decision; service credentials in integration-corev2 scoped per room binding, with the team copy re-requesting owner-plane grants.
items.planeOwner: Model Plane (agent definitions, sandboxes) with Control Plane decisions
items.risks: A central grants table would be cross-plane DB access. Carrying credentials would break agents not sharing credentials; memory carry-over can leak personal data. Packages in manifests are a supply-chain risk. Single-source, partly medium-confidence evidence.

verevon.exactGap: No team layer, no scope-to-scope grants for Space resources, no setup manifests and no publish-to-team exist, and ResolvedSpaceContext has zero code hits (docs only): the real context assembly is the gateway's inject_authored_instructions plus fetch_org/space_instructions and the agent persona, composed in model-gateway. Control has team and team_member tables in auth-core but nothing links teams to Spaces, instructions or policy, and agent definitions are per-org with per-Space bindings and no personal owner scope. Capability-core has an explicit scope-grant store (run|thread|workspace|user|org|global) with no team or space kind, and the Space authority ADR classes its workspace scope as unsupported for Space until a controlled resolver exists.
evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:3700-3780 (Space instruction role floor editor/manager/owner; read by any member)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:4225-4300 (fetch_org_instructions, fetch_space_instructions, inject_authored_instructions: org and Space layers resolved server-side)
apps/AUTHORED_INSTRUCTIONS_ADR_2026-08-19.md:1-60 (ADR-0003 implemented; platform+org+Space+agent persona; QM's own mechanism is two layers)
apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/schema.ts:318-410 (agents table is per-org; createdBy optional; no personal scope)
apps/Application Plane/convex-core/convex/spaceAgents.ts:195-260 (org-wide installation registry, presence not authority)
apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/db/schema.ts:238-275 (team, team_member tables; invitation teamId)
apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/repository.go:660-680,750-775 (personal Space membership cannot be replaced; roster sync must not destroy agent bindings)

apps/SPACE_AUTHORITY_ADR_2026-08-13.md:40-110 (effective access = Space decision intersect audience intersect owner-plane authz; personal Space content/credentials/memory never reused across memberships; capability-core workspace scope not live Space support)
apps/Control Plane/auth-core/src/internal/internal-agent-signup.controller.ts:1-60 (agent-signup is Quarry provisioning a sandbox account, not agent service accounts)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/roadmap/data.go:55-80 (stale: marks sandbox-manager not implemented although lease/workspace/snapshot/process internals exist)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/sandbox-manager/internal/workspace/store.go:1-40 (sandbox substrate where setup manifests would hook in)
reuse: ADR-0003 authored-instruction composition (gateway inject_authored_instructions, Convex instructionsForGateway queries, model-gateway composition) as the place to add a team layer
Control auth-core team/team_member tables as the team source once Teams (F-t1-054) land
capability-core scope-grant store as the Model Plane precedent for skill grants (add kinds only after a controlled Space resolver exists)
agentInstallationsForOrgForGateway registry (ADR-0002) for 'where is this agent bound'
sandbox-manager lease and workspace manifest for setup manifests at sandbox creation
plane service-principal pattern (Auth Core PLANE_SERVICE_PRINCIPALS_JSON, mail_task_bridge_auth) for scoped service credentials
verevon.constraints: Space membership never widens a resource ACL, so team-layer instructions (authored text) are fine but team-layer resource handles must pass the Space decision intersected with the owner-plane check; grants stay in the owning plane, never a central table (no cross-plane DB access). A personal Space's content, credentials and memory are never reused across org memberships and a personal Space has exactly one subject, so publish-to-team must be an explicit, owner-confirmed copy that never carries credentials or personal chats. Setup manifests must run through the Control-signed, backend-pinned sandbox lease and an allowlisted package registry (supply chain). Per-agent service credentials need an integration-corev2 ownership design: today credentials are either plane service principals or the user's own OAuth tokens.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Name the real seam: there is no ResolvedSpaceContext struct to extend, so the team layer is an addition to the ADR-0003 authored-instruction composition (a teams-aware Convex instructions query, the gateway injector, model-gateway composition), blocked on Control Teams being linked to Spaces. Split into (A) team instruction layer (M), (B) setup manifests in sandbox-manager (L, Model Plane), and (C) publish-to-team plus agent service accounts (XL), and demote (C): it needs personal agents, which do not exist (inference, low confidence: agent definitions have no owner scope and I found no code that binds an agent into a personal Space either way). Do not reuse capability-core's workspace scope for Space until the controlled resolver exists.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged as a bundle, but only (A) is near-term; (B) and (C) depend on Teams, personal agents and the agent access list.
verevon.verdictReason: The instruction hierarchy already exists and is mis-framed as a missing ResolvedSpaceContext; the genuinely missing parts (team layer, manifests, promotion, agent credentials) are correctly absent but should be split by readiness, with the promotion half demoted.

items.title: Tauri desktop shell around the gateway origin: narrow bridge, system-browser sign-in, protocol links, signed updater
items.summary: After the PWA, build a Tauri 2 shell that loads the existing gateway origin with a locked CSP and no local tokens, exposes a versioned, schema-validated bridge of at most about 15 capability commands (notify, badge, open-external, deep-link, window state, updater status), and signs users in through the system browser with a single-use PKCE handoff that mints the same HttpOnly BFF session in an isolated webview profile. Register a native verevon:// protocol with single-instance forwarding and a cold-start queue feeding the F-t1-039 (R-t1-11-03) router, and ship signed MSIX/MSI/DMG installers with a gateway-served updater manifest that installs only when no agent run is streaming and no draft is unsent.
items.whyItMatters: All five references ship a native shell, and it is the only route to tray presence, OS protocol links from mail and Office, and global hotkeys. Verevon can capture most value with the PWA first, but enterprise rollout (IT-managed installers, "chat with" links) eventually needs this.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: teams (thin native shell around a web UI with a versioned RPC over capability modules); buzz (Tauri 2, Rust-owned state) is the closest stack fit
others: slack (one URL grammar on every OS, should-i-update server decision, Joi-validated bridge channels)
qm (PKCE desktop handoff, locked-down minimal Electron shell)
grokbot (never install while an agent is working)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Shell 5 of 5, protocol handler 5 of 5, bridge 4 of 5, updater 4 of 5, signed packaging 4 of 5 = table-stakes; system-browser sign-in 3 of 5 = common.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Shell loads the remote web app in a system WebView; renderer sandboxed with a narrow typed bridge (single envelope, per-capability schemas, sender-origin check, validation-failure telemetry); native side owns badge, notifications, deep links, updates. Tauri 2 plugins: single-instance, deep-link, window-state, updater, notification. PKCE: app creates verifier and state, opens /auth/desktop?challenge, the portal returns a sealed two-minute code through the protocol link, the app redeems it with the verifier for a session cookie. Updater: idle, checking, staging, ready; apply on idle; block while runs or uploads are active; candidate-commit CI with signed canary then promote.

verevonToday.gap: Web SPA only: no Electron, Tauri or MSIX package, no tray, native notifications, protocol handler, bridge, updater or desktop sign-in (SRC plus a dated internal audit, DOC, which calls Windows presence greenfield). Only HTTPS routes exist; the BFF cookie session is the right target for the handoff.

items.approach: Frontend Plane: new desktop workspace in verevonv3 (Tauri 2, Rust to match the gateway stack) with a capability ACL file and a shared TS/Rust bridge schema in packages/; native protocol and single-instance handling that parse into the same route table as F-t1-039 (R-t1-11-03) with an allowlist of commands. Control Plane identity plus the gateway: /auth/desktop PKCE endpoint minting a sealed single-use short-TTL code bound to challenge, state and audience. Gateway: updater manifest per org and channel (stable/beta) with rollback and update-required hints from F-t1-024 (R-t1-11-04). CI: Tauri bundler for MSIX/MSI and DMG using a candidate-commit release pattern and held signing certificates. No local agent runtime and no offline message store: agent execution stays server-side under "Model proposes, Quarry executes", which keeps audit and ZDR intact.
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (sign-in handoff: Control Plane)
items.risks: Code-signing and notarisation custody and cost; a second client to test; bridge sprawl enlarges the attack surface (Slack has 122 channels, Teams about 545 methods), so keep it minimal; link parsing is an injection surface; a broken update channel strands users, so rollback is mandatory; no local caching of Space content that would break ZDR.

verevon.exactGap: No desktop shell of any kind exists: the Frontend Plane is a Vite SPA with no manifest or service worker, no Tauri, Electron or MSIX files exist outside node_modules, the gateway has no desktop sign-in, protocol-link or updater endpoint, and auth-core has no PKCE or code-challenge route. The only native code in the monorepo is Endpoint Plane's verevon-agent, a Rust remote-desktop host whose own docs list packaging and installer as out of scope, and .github/workflows holds no signing or installer pipeline. Notifications are in-app only (gateway notifications.rs list, unread and preference routes), so tray, badge and OS notification bridges are also absent.
reuse: BFF cookie session: auth-core Better Auth proxied by gateway upstream.rs with tokens held only in HttpOnly cookies
existing in-app deep links (SpaceCockpit tabFromHash, chat thread deep-link parser) as the route table the protocol handler must feed
Endpoint Plane Rust workspace conventions (forbid unsafe, rfd consent prompt) and a future shared signing and update pipeline
gateway notifications.rs feed and unread count as the data behind a native badge
verevon.constraints: Frontend Plane owns the shell, but the desktop sign-in handoff is Control Plane (auth-core) work because the session is a Better Auth HttpOnly cookie minted behind the gateway and no PKCE endpoint exists. The shell must keep no local agent runtime or offline Space cache so Model proposes, Quarry executes, audit and ZDR stay server-side. The active organization is session state (orgs/switch.rs:58), so protocol links must carry org context and handle the wrong-org case, and the nginx CSP frame-ancestors none is compatible with a top-level webview but would block any embedding approach.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Keep as written, with two additions: the installer, signing and update pipeline is fully greenfield (Endpoint Plane's verevon-agent also lacks packaging, so one pipeline could serve both), and the PKCE handoff needs a new auth-core endpoint rather than a gateway-only change.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged: native shell, bridge, protocol handling, sign-in handoff, signed installers and an update channel are all new.
verevon.verdictReason: The shell is accurately described as absent, nothing in the repo already covers it, and the proposed plane placement matches the session and CSP constraints.

items.title: Provenance footer on relayed and automated messages and notifications; optional system voice
items.summary: Carry {sender_agent, on_behalf_of, trigger: reply, cron or relay, schedule_ref} on posts and notification payloads, and render a footer such as 'sent for @person' or the schedule name with a link back to the schedule settings. As an optional second phase, give platform notices (policy changes, new Space features) one system sender identity with a per-user cap and opt-out.
items.whyItMatters: It prevents confusion about who an automated message speaks for and fits Verevon's authority model, where owner effect receipts and authorising grants are already recorded. In a room full of agents and scheduled runs, a user needs to know whether a ping came from a person, an agent acting for a person, or a cron.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (provenance); Grok Bot for system-voice announcements
others: Slack (Slackbot as single voice for notices and reminders)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Provenance: 1 of 5 sources, unique; system voice: 2 of 5, differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: QM sets a relaySender field when attributeAs differs from the sender, renders a footer, and records the trigger in delivery provenance. Grok Bot delivers changelog items through the bot with relevance guidance, delivery windows, eligibility gates, a minimum client version and a maximum number of offers; the agent decides whether to mention them in a relevant conversation.

verevonToday.gap: The room Activity feed already shows owner effect receipts and the grants that authorised them, but a grep of src/features/spaces and spaces.rs found no on-behalf-of, relay-sender or trigger fields on posts or notifications (INF). Whether schedule-run posts in conversation-core carry an attribution field was not checked, and no system sender identity for platform notices was found.

items.approach: Application Plane: add on_behalf_of and trigger to the post model and to the F-t1-008 (R-t1-05-01) notification payload; reuse the grants and receipts already in Activity as the source. Frontend Plane: render the provenance footer on timeline posts, inbox items and toasts. Phase 2 (Model Plane plus Control): an announcement store the user's agent can consult, gated by Control eligibility and capped per user, only after the footer ships.
dependencies: Schedule-run post attribution check in conversation-core
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (provenance); Model Plane and Control (system voice, phase 2)
items.risks: System-voice announcements can feel like ads inside an agent, so cap and allow opt-out; attribution fields must come from the server, never from the browser.

verevon.exactGap: Server-recorded provenance already exists but is not projected to the room: each message stores author_subject_id and agent_name, threads relay an origin field, and scheduled runs record source scheduled_run, schedule_id, fire_key and the creating human's subject_id in run metadata plus cron_schedules.creator_subject_id; however SpaceThread has no origin, schedule or on-behalf-of fields, schedule threads are owned by service:orchestrator-core and the timeline's resolveAuthorName has no case for a service principal (a roster miss reads as 'former member', INF), and the Work tab only links to Settings for routines. No relay or on-behalf-of concept exists (web is the only active surface, S5 adapters are gated), notification-core has actor fields and a free-form payload but no Space-event producers (its producers are conversation follow, mail-task and social-publish), and no system sender identity or announcement store exists.
evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/shared/api/spaces-client.ts:36-65 (SpaceThread type: owner_subject_id, status, pin; no origin or schedule)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/grpc.rs:2252 (THREAD_ORIGINS: chat, space, agent_run, support, system, mail_task)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/session-core/src/grpc.rs:1380-1420 (run metadata source scheduled_run, schedule_id, fire_key, subject_id)
apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/personal_thread_decision.go:205-235 (schedule result thread is system-owned, created by a trusted service)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/spaces.rs:1349-1375 (Activity shows owner effects and the grants that authorised them)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpaceWorkPanel.tsx:140-185 (routines managed in Settings, link to /settings/cron)
apps/Application Plane/notification-core/internal/feed/types.go:30-47,85-95 (Notification and CreateParams: ActorID, ActorName, ActorEmail, free-form Payload)

Grep of apps for system_sender|announcement|platform notice: no matches (negative; scan result)
reuse: run metadata {source, schedule_id, fire_key, subject_id} already written for scheduled runs
ThreadSummary.origin relay through model-gateway and the existing gateway thread passthrough
SpaceWorkPanel schedules list and the /settings/cron link for the 'open schedule' target
Space roster for naming the on-behalf-of human (membership-bound)
notification-core Actor fields and Payload map for notification provenance
verevon.constraints: Posts and messages live in Session Core (Model Plane), not the Application Plane, so the item's plane assignment for the post part is wrong; notifications are Application Plane (notification-core). Provenance must be server-derived from recorded metadata, never browser-supplied (migration 0035 sets the same rule). On-behalf-of names must be resolved through the Space roster so a footer does not reveal a creator to readers who cannot see members. ZDR: provenance is metadata only and ZDR attempts stay content-free. Web is the only active surface (S5 gated), so a 'relay' trigger has no producer yet. The Space definition's non-goals (no auto-responding agents, notification polish) argue against the system-voice phase.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Derive the footer from data already recorded: have Session Core expose the latest run's source, schedule_id and creator subject on the thread summary (model-gateway relays it, the gateway passes it through), and render 'Scheduled run: <schedule name> for <creator>' in SpaceRoomTimeline with a link to the schedule in Settings; name service principals explicitly instead of falling through to 'former member'. Add trigger and on_behalf_of to notification payloads only when Space-event producers exist (F-t1-008). Drop the relay field until a relay surface exists and drop the system-voice phase 2 (no infrastructure and in tension with the non-goals).
verevon.effortNote: Lowered from M for the recommended slice (room-post footer for scheduled runs) because the provenance is already stored; the notification-payload part waits on F-t1-008 and system voice is dropped.
verevon.verdictReason: Partially real and cheaper than stated: the provenance already exists in run metadata and thread origin and only needs projecting to the room, the post model is in Session Core not the Application Plane, and the relay and system-voice parts have no producer or infrastructure, so reduce to a scheduled-run footer now.

items.title: Agent external channels: per-agent email first, then Slack and Teams apps
items.summary: Phase 1: finish the mail-task pipeline into a per-agent address. Inbound mail is verified and deduped in Ingestion Plane, then wakes the agent as an untrusted unattended turn; outbound send is an approval-gated integration action. Phase 2 (after the durable delivery ledger and a real Channel Plane): publish an agent into Slack or Teams as its own app with an install-state machine, external messages entering under the installing user's authority.
items.whyItMatters: Gives personal agents a human-like identity and an async intake, and meets users where they already chat, a strong adoption lever for Teams-heavy companies. The email front half is already built, and the unblocking steps are documented in code, so phase 1 is a finishing job rather than a new system.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Slack/Teams agent apps: 2 of 5 (grokbot, qm; differentiator); per-agent email: Grok Bot only (unique)
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Grok Bot creates a Slack app per bot through the manifest API (scopes for mentions, DMs, files, reactions, interactivity), installs it through OAuth with a typed outcome INSTALLED|PENDING_ADMIN_APPROVAL|WORKSPACE_REQUIRED|INSUFFICIENT_SCOPES|INSTALL_CONFLICT|RATELIMITED, and uses a per-tenant package for Teams. Outbound channels are typed addresses (email, Slack, Teams, SMS). Email: a dedicated domain per bot, mail only wakes the bot through a user routine, sending is approval-gated, and admins get sending windows, suppression lists and stats. qm's single-app manifest with an Agents pin is the simpler alternative.

verevonToday.gap: Mail-to-task is a self-forward flow (Postmark inbound): Ingestion and the gateway verify, rate-limit and dedup, then the gateway always returns 503 mail_task_pipeline_not_configured, because no unattended (no-live-user) turn exists outside Space scheduled runs. The thread-preparation seam (a mail_task_thread_bridge client for model-gateway's prepare-thread route over session-core PrepareUserOwnedThread) is built but deliberately unwired (SRC; module docs dated 2026-09-28, may be newer in code). No per-agent address and no send. Slack/Teams: a delivery-target field exists on bindings (stub, internal mutation only) and agent cards display targets; there is no adapter or install flow, the Slack/Teams mirror is planned (S5.1 ADR adopted, S5.3 blocked behind S4.4 and S4.3) and Channel Plane is docs-only.

items.approach: Phase 1 (Ingestion Plane plus Model Plane): reuse the mailtask verify, dedup and resolver path; wire the existing thread bridge (Auth Core service principal for the gateway, model-gateway internal route) and, sharing the unattended-turn plumbing with F-t1-047 (R-t1-06-03), post the synthesized first turn as untrusted input under the owner's authority; add a per-agent address claim; outbound send is a Model-proposed, room-approved integration action with suppression and rate windows. Phase 2: stand up Channel Plane only after S4.4 durable delivery, one adapter per platform, per-agent app identity, an install-state machine modelled on Grok Bot's outcome enum, a Control-owned external-identity link graph (never match on email alone, per the S5.1 ADR), and blocked delivery for ZDR Spaces because content leaves the boundary.
dependencies: Auth Core service principal for model-gateway
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane (inbound email); Application Plane (delivery targets and mapping); Control Plane (identity links); Channel Plane (future adapters)
items.risks: Spam and phishing reaching agents (prompt injection through mail bodies); deliverability; ZDR violations when content leaves the boundary; platform review and admin-approval friction; identity mapping between external users and Verevon principals.

verevon.constraints: The mail-task design is an owner ruling of self-forward only (sender must be the verified owner), so a per-agent address that wakes an agent from arbitrary senders reverses that ruling and opens a prompt-injection surface; the existing Control decision is purpose-built for one user-owned thread and deliberately has no Space authority, so an agent in a Space needs a Space-bound decision. The only unattended-turn precedent is the Space scheduled run, whose bounded runtime is tool-free and not yet safe for effects, so email-triggered tool use needs approval. ZDR: mail_task threads are persisted content (principal retention persistent), so ZDR orgs must be refused for inbound wake and for external delivery. Control owns the external-identity link graph and Application owns delivery and receipts (S5.1 ADR); S4.4 delivery is source-only and Channel Plane is docs-only. Outbound today sends as the user, so an agent-owned sender identity needs an integration-corev2 credential ownership design.

Add email and slack to the deliveryTargets channel union (Convex schema change) before any adapter. Phase 2 stays as proposed (S5.1 then S5.3, Slack first per the plan), with blocked delivery for ZDR Spaces.
