verevon.exactGap: None of the three proposals exists, only foundations: presence is already gated on tab visibility with a 6 s beat (SpacePage.tsx:206-250, Convex presence TTL 30 s and typing 8 s) but has no input-idle or away state, navbar and notification unread counts are computed for the active organization only (notifications.rs unread_count, navbar.rs unreadCount), and the org switcher lists organizations without counts (CoreNavbar.tsx:685-735). There is no pop-out or compact route: window.open appears only for provider sign-in, search results and Knowledge links, and AgentRunConsole is a page-level component with local state that takes no run id parameter, although it can replay a chosen history run through streamRunEvents (AgentRunConsole.tsx:329). Nothing coordinates tabs (no BroadcastChannel, SharedWorker or Web Locks), and the active organization is server-side session state (orgs/switch.rs:58), so every window in a browser shares one active org.
reuse: streamRunEvents with lastEventId resume and the run-event rendering in AgentRunConsole as the pop-out body once extracted
Space transcript route and SpaceRoomPost for a pop-out thread view
the beat() presence path in SpacePage.tsx and spaces.record_presence, extended with an away state
CoreNavbar workspace switcher rows and listOrganizations for per-org badges
gateway notifications.rs and notification-core unread count, called per org
verevon.constraints: Active org is session state, so a pop-out cannot show a different org than the main window, and per-org unread must be computed server-side by the gateway for each of the user's Control memberships under that org's own authorization (counts only, never Space names, in the switcher). Presence is personal data and must stay optional, and adding an away status is an Application Plane change (current status enum is online or typing). A shared connection or leader tab is premature because Space data is polled and only per-turn chat and run-event streams exist.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Build in this order: pop-out routes (extract a props-driven run view and add a compact layout flag with run or thread id params), an idle or away presence signal derived from visibility plus input idle in beat(), then a gateway per-org unread-count endpoint feeding the switcher. Defer the SharedWorker or BroadcastChannel multiplexer until a persistent push subscription exists; if duplicate 6 s polls matter sooner, share the polled projection across tabs through BroadcastChannel instead of multiplexing SSE.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged overall but uneven: pop-out S to M, idle signal S, cross-org unread M (per-org authorization), leader-tab multiplexing deferred.
verevon.verdictReason: The proposal is accurate that these are missing, but it should drop the SSE multiplexer until a push stream exists, note the shared active-org constraint, and recognise that visibility-gated presence already exists.

items.title: Shell-only conveniences: quick composer, global hotkey and push-to-talk, window state, close guard
items.summary: Once the Tauri shell exists, add an always-on-top mini composer window that posts to the same gateway run endpoint as the Space composer (landing in the user's personal Space so it stays auditable), a validated global shortcut with key-up events for push-to-talk to the voice feature, and window-state memory. Ship the web-first part now: a beforeunload guard when the Space composer holds unsent text or a run is awaiting approval.
items.whyItMatters: A personal agent one keystroke away is the Grok Bot half of the Space vision, and push-to-talk suits the existing voice feature. These need OS-level hooks a browser tab cannot provide.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: grokbot (transparent always-on-top mini composer that sends to the selected Bot, switchable from a menu)
others: slack (flag-gated tray-click overlay; validated global-shortcut API with key-down/key-up; bounds clamped to a live display)
teams (close prompts for unsent messages and calls)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Window management 3 of 5 (common); quick composer 2 of 5 (differentiator); global shortcuts 1 of 5 (unique).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Frameless transparent window loading a minimal composer route with its own capability set and a typed call that submits a prompt to the selected agent; native global-shortcut registration with validation and key-up events; persisted bounds per window type validated against live displays; close policy with prompt cases.

verevonToday.gap: No native shell, so no window management, global shortcuts or quick composer; a web equivalent of the close prompt (beforeunload on unsent composer text or a running agent) was not found.

items.approach: Frontend Plane inside the F-t1-073 (R-t1-11-09) workspace: secondary window plus tauri-plugin-global-shortcut and tauri-plugin-window-state; the mini composer route posts through the existing run endpoint with org and ZDR context carried; push-to-talk reuses src/features/voice. Web-first guard is a small beforeunload handler on the Space composer. Overlaps in-tab push-to-talk keys in F-t1-086 (R-t1-03-11).
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Prompts typed outside a Space must still carry ZDR and org context; shortcut collisions with other apps; over-eager beforeunload prompts annoy users.

verevon.exactGap: No native shell exists: index.html is a plain web entry, the parity audit confirms no Electron or Tauri app and no PWA manifest, Endpoint Plane is a native Rust remote-desktop host agent rather than a chat shell, and apps/remote-dev is a dev harness. The web-first close guard is also absent, since verevonv3 has no beforeunload or pagehide handler and SpaceRoomComposer neither persists drafts nor warns on unsent text or a running own stream. The scan candidate start_ai_run in browser.rs is the browser-agent run route, not the Space composer endpoint, which is the chat stream and AG-UI routes with Space context injection.
reuse: SpaceRoomComposer streamChat path through gateway chat/streams.rs and ag_ui.rs, which already inject Control-issued Space decisions from a space_ref alone
space-live-work ownStream and Space approval state to decide when a close guard is warranted
voice-recorder and VoiceModeDialog for push-to-talk once a key-up event is available
verevon.constraints: The browser may choose only space_ref and the gateway strips every forged authority field (FORGED_SPACE_AUTHORITY_FIELDS), so a quick composer must go through the same Space-injection path and land in the personal Space, never a separate run API with client-authored authority. ZDR and org context are applied server-side on that shared path (apply_org_zdr_posture after the Space injectors) from the validated session, so the shell webview must reuse the session and must not hold its own credentials. The shell depends on F-t1-073 and nothing in the repo provides it today. Global push-to-talk and always-on-top windows are shell-only; the close guard is a Frontend Plane web change.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into (1) a web-first guard, S: beforeunload when the Space composer holds unsent text or an own stream is running, optionally with draft persistence, shippable now; and (2) the shell-only quick composer, global shortcut and window state, which wait for F-t1-073 and should target the chat stream and AG-UI routes, not browser.rs start_ai_run. Define push-to-talk once with F-t1-086 rather than twice.
verevon.effortNote: M for the shell-only conveniences assuming the shell exists (the shell itself is XL elsewhere); the web-first guard is S and a quick win.
verevon.verdictReason: Absent is right for the shell part, but the item misses that the web-first guard is also unbuilt, and its implied endpoint (the scan pointed at the browser-agent run route) is wrong; split the cheap web slice from the shell-gated slice.

items.title: Realtime and media operability after push ships: shared connection per browser, drain on deploy, capability discovery, stream-stall self-test, perf marks, media cache policy
items.summary: Once the push stream exists: share one connection across tabs (leader tab via Web Locks and BroadcastChannel, or SharedWorker) with frame batching; autoscale on active connections and drain with a close frame plus client resume; advertise capabilities and limits in the connected frame; add a diagnostics stream with timed heartbeats so the client detects SSE buffering by customer proxies and shows IT guidance; report web vitals and a space_open mark; and verify the media route supports Range, ETag and private caching with no-store for ZDR Spaces.
items.whyItMatters: Operational hardening that matters only after the substrate ships; Verevon's own nginx tier is already stream-friendly, so the risk sits in customer networks.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Buzz (shared socket with frame coalescing, HPA on active-websocket gauge, NIP-11 capability document); Slack for drain (cell and AZ drain in about 5 minutes; DOC); QM for ack-after-durable ingress (AckGate, 2.5 s cap, durable staging, redelivery on failure) and single background-owner record; grokbot (in-app Network Debugger with IT guidance for SSE and HTTP/2) for network diagnostics; teams (shared scenario marks and INP-style telemetry) for performance; buzz (media grants with range requests) for media
others: Teams (shared workers, BroadcastChannel and Web Locks across windows; published limits with feature degradation by room size)
Grok Bot (about 260 typed dynamic configs with client fallbacks; utility-process coordinator over MessagePort)
buzz (Playwright suite and E2E bridge that mocks transport)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: [R-t1-09-11] 3 of 5 for off-thread/shared sync, scale-out and protocol evolution (common); 2 of 5 for load shaping and ack-after-durable ingress (differentiator); 1 of 5 for server-driven tuning [R-t1-11-12] Network diagnostics 2 of 5, startup performance 2 of 5, authenticated media 2 of 5 = differentiators.
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: [R-t1-09-11] Web equivalent: a leader tab elected via Web Locks owns the single SSE and posts coalesced batches to other tabs over BroadcastChannel. HPA on the active-connection gauge; on deploy the old build stops claiming and sends close frames so clients reconnect with resume. GET capabilities or a connected-frame field lists supported features and limits and absence means unsupported. A registry maps config name to schema and fallback. Ingress holds the platform ack until the event is persisted, or after a cap writes the raw envelope to a durable map and acks. [R-t1-11-12] Connectivity probe classes (DNS, TLS, proxy, stream stall) with remediation text; scenarioStart/Mark/Stop emitting success, failure or abandoned; media URLs carry short-lived authorization and forward Range headers with a content-keyed cache.

verevonToday.gap: [R-t1-09-11] SRC: timings are hard-coded constants (6 s poll, 30 s recheck); a per-tab store avoids duplicate polls within a tab but no BroadcastChannel, Web Locks or SharedWorker usage was found outside demo files; the gateway /api/v1/capabilities route is the Model Plane skills catalog, not realtime capability discovery; agent-binding delivery targets are a schema stub and Channel Plane is docs-only. Unknown: gateway replica and autoscaling manifests, leader election for background loops, room size limits, and cron jitter in capability-core. [R-t1-11-12] The SSE reader supports Last-Event-ID resume but a grep of sse.ts finds no heartbeat, stall or timeout detection and no connectivity self-test. The Verevon-owned nginx tier is already stream-friendly (proxy_buffering off, 3600 s read timeout on /api/), so the risk sits in customer-side proxies and TLS inspection. Performance telemetry, route-level chunking intent and the media route (Range support, cache headers, ZDR no-store) were not assessed. Playwright configs including a real-authority one exist; a scripted SSE fixture for Space events was not found.

items.approach: [R-t1-09-11] After F-t1-003 (R-t1-09-01): (1) leader-tab connection manager in the SPA (SharedWorker is limited on iOS Safari, so prefer Web Locks); (2) check gateway deployment manifests for replicas and HPA metric and add an active-connection gauge, drain with close frame and jittered resume; (3) add features and limits to the stream connected frame, with an ignore-unknown-kinds rule in the client; (4) move poll and watchdog timings into one typed config registry (overlaps feature flags in F-t1-006 (R-t1-02-05)) with fallbacks; (5) coalesce per-room fan-out above a member threshold and add jitter to capability-core cron; (6) when Channel Plane or F-t1-075 (R-t1-06-10) external channels start, apply ack-after-durable staging. [R-t1-11-12] Frontend Plane: /diagnostics/stream endpoint in the gateway plus a stall detector in sse.ts and a settings-page self-test with an allowlist document; web-vitals and space_open marks posted to the monitoring domain; audit the gateway media route for cookie auth, Range, ETag, private cache-control and no-store for ZDR; optional scripted SSE fixture so Playwright can assert agent-activity rendering deterministically.
dependencies: F-t1-035 (R-t1-11-01) (service-worker shell cache, if perf marks compare cached and cold opens)
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane (gateway and SPA) with Application Plane (load shaping)
items.risks: [R-t1-09-11] Reconnect storms after drain need jitter. Config sprawl if the registry is not kept small. SharedWorker support gaps on some browsers. [R-t1-11-12] Stale service-worker caches skew perf data; caching private media on shared machines; mock fixtures drifting from real contracts.

verevon.exactGap: Server-side operability is further along than the item assumes: model-gateway already drains on SIGTERM (drain.rs, 120 s default, readyz 503), exports a gateway_active_streams gauge, emits 15 s keep-alive comment frames and a content-free turn_timing event, so the missing pieces are on the client and the Frontend Plane gateway. The SPA reader skips comment frames (sse.ts:106) so there is no stall or buffering detection, nothing shares a connection across tabs (no BroadcastChannel, SharedWorker, Web Locks, Idle Detection or PerformanceObserver in src), the connected frame carries only ok, request_id, run_id, thread_id and model (sse.rs:2165), and the Frontend gateway serves with axum::serve and no graceful shutdown (main.rs:82, compose stop_grace_period 20 s). Much of it is premature for Spaces: the room has no push stream (6 s visible-tab poll, SpacePage.tsx:87), the Space composer has no attachments or media route so the Range, ETag and no-store slice has nothing to apply to, and the monitoring domain the item names for vitals is Quarry change monitoring, not telemetry.
reuse: model-gateway drain.rs pattern (readyz 503, wait for registered streams, bounded window) for the Frontend gateway
server keep-alive comment frames (sse.rs with_keep_alive, ag_ui.rs KeepAlive) as the liveness signal for a client watchdog
gateway observability.rs Prometheus recorder for vitals and space_open counters and histograms
turn_timing.rs content-free timing record as the model for ZDR-safe client telemetry
space-live-work.ts module store and the existing visibilitychange gating in SpacePage.tsx
Last-Event-ID resume already implemented in sse.ts, chat-client.ts and run-console-client.ts
verevon.constraints: New SSE events or connected-frame fields are CI-gated: the SPA chat-client.ts and the taxonomy doc must agree with sse_events.rs (sse-taxonomy.yml). Capability advertisement belongs to Model Plane's connected frame, telemetry to the Frontend gateway observability layer, and neither may carry content under ZDR. Any media route added later must send no-store for ZDR Spaces and re-check Space authority on every Range request, and a leader-tab multiplexer has nothing persistent to multiplex until Spaces have a push subscription.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split into build-now and after-push. Build now: make readSseStream surface comment frames as a liveness tick and arm a stall watchdog (the server already sends the heartbeats, so no new diagnostics stream is needed except for an optional IT self-test); add graceful shutdown and a stream gauge to the Frontend gateway by copying model-gateway drain.rs and raising stop_grace_period; post vitals and space_open marks through a small gateway telemetry route backed by observability.rs, not the monitoring domain. After push ships: leader-tab sharing and capability fields in the connected frame. Drop the media cache slice until Space attachments exist.
verevon.effortNote: Buildable now is S (watchdog), S (gateway drain), S to M (vitals); leader-tab sharing is M and deferred until a persistent subscription exists, and the media slice is dropped.
verevon.verdictReason: Heartbeats, drain and an active-stream gauge already exist in model-gateway, the named vitals target is the wrong domain, and the media and leader-tab slices have no substrate yet, so the item needs rewording and splitting rather than keeping as is.

items.title: Delivery health: channel failover and a 'why am I not notified' diagnosis
items.summary: Track per-device and per-channel health {consecutive_failures, failover_at} in the S4.4 ledger and fall back along an order such as push, then in-app, then email digest, retrying the primary after a TTL. Pair it with a Settings and bell banner that lists typed reasons notifications are not arriving (DND active, browser permission denied, push subscription expired, room muted, channel failing), computed client-side for browser state and server-side for preferences and last failed attempt.
items.whyItMatters: Cuts support load and builds trust that agent alerts will arrive. Silent channel switching confuses users unless it is paired with a diagnosis, which is why the two belong together. Only worthwhile after push and email exist.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Slack (only source)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5 sources; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Slack keeps a consecutive-failure counter (5 triggers telemetry), records a failover timestamp for a week and clears it at the next start so the native path is retried, and policy can force native. Its warning call returns typed reason codes, cached 30 s when warnings exist and 1 h when clean.

verevonToday.gap: notification-core records per-attempt status but a grep of its Go sources found no failover or channel-health logic, and no per-user delivery-status or diagnostics endpoint was found in its HTTP routes (INF from grep).

items.approach: Application Plane: add channel health and fallback order to the ledger from F-t1-060 (R-t1-05-10), plus a read endpoint exposing server-side reasons (preferences, DND, last failed attempt). Frontend Plane: compute browser-side reasons (permission, subscription) and show a banner in Settings and next to the bell.
items.planeOwner: Application Plane (health state); Frontend Plane (banner)
items.risks: Low; silent failover without the diagnosis would confuse users. The Space definition treats notification polish as a non-goal (docs/space-defenition.md:352-353).

verevon.exactGap: No failover, channel-health or diagnostics code exists: notification-core's delivery ledger (pending, claimed, sent_unconfirmed, acknowledged, failed, unknown, with a worker behind DeliveryWorkerEnabled) tracks Novu provider submissions per notification, not per-device or per-channel health, and its HTTP routes expose only feed, preferences and channel configs. The frontend has no browser push, permission or service-worker code, so push-expired and permission-denied states cannot occur yet, and the only notification empty state is 'Connect Novu'. Quiet hours exist only as a default in user-core settings that notification-core does not read.
evidence: apps/Application Plane/notification-core/internal/notification/delivery_state.go:1-60 (per-attempt status enum and queue; ambiguous outcomes not retried blindly)
apps/Application Plane/notification-core/cmd/server/main.go:179-224 (delivery worker and feed projection worker behind DeliveryWorkerEnabled)
apps/Application Plane/notification-core/internal/http/server.go:55-100 (routes: feed, preferences, channel configs, provider callback; no delivery-status or diagnostics route)
apps/Application Plane/notification-core/internal/runtime/client.go:195-230 (channel toggles mapped to Novu; no fallback order)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/notifications.rs:19-31 (preferences, unread, list, read, delete only)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md:2205-2224 (S4.4 delivery ledger plan includes preferences and quiet hours, web first)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/space-defenition.md:345-358 (non-goals: no chat-feature parity race including notification polish)
Grep of apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src for requestPermission|pushManager|serviceWorker|new Notification(: only src/demo/product-demo/guard.ts (negative)
reuse: notification-core DeliveryAttempt ledger and worker as the base for per-channel failure counts
notification-core preferences and channel-config routes
gateway notifications proxy routes for a future read-only diagnostics endpoint
user-core quietHours default as the source for a DND reason once notification-core honours it
verevon.constraints: Notification-core is Application Plane and delivery runs through Novu, which owns channel mechanics, so failover order is more naturally a Novu workflow concern than custom Verevon logic (INF). ZDR: ledger rows must stay content-free (already true of DeliveryAttempt). Diagnostics must be computed from server-owned preferences and last-failed attempts plus browser state computed client-side; the browser must not assert delivery state. The Space definition lists notification polish as a non-goal.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not build this before web push, a Space notification producer and quiet-hours enforcement exist; none do. When they do, ship the diagnosis banner first (client-computed permission and subscription state plus a server read of preferences, DND and last failed attempt) and treat automatic channel failover as optional, preferring Novu's own fallback configuration over a custom ledger-driven failover.
verevon.effortNote: Raised from S: S assumed push, preferences and a per-channel ledger exist; the ledger is per-attempt for Novu and push is absent. The diagnosis banner alone is S once push exists; failover is the M part.
verevon.verdictReason: Absent, single-source (Slack only), and premature: it presupposes browser push, enforced quiet hours and Space notification producers that do not exist, and the Space definition treats notification polish as a non-goal. Keep it as a later nice-to-have behind push.

items.title: Multi-org and external collaboration horizon: org archive and transfer, shared cross-org rooms, managed external chat connections
items.summary: Do the cheap part first: org lifecycle states (archived, owner transfer) in org-core. Later, after guests, add org-to-org links with host-org-owned shared rooms and external trust cues, with QM's rule that an external audience restricts agents to a context without org memory or keys. External chat workspace connections belong to the future Channel Plane, not to be built elsewhere.
items.whyItMatters: Slack Connect and Teams shared channels are enterprise differentiators, and a parent org over several orgs matters for managed-service customers. Verevon's customers are single companies today, so this is a long-horizon investment; org archive and transfer are the useful cheap slice.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: slack (Enterprise Grid, Slack Connect), buzz (operator lifecycle), qm (external audience isolation, managed Slack connections)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: tenant hierarchy 2 of 5, shared channels 3 of 5 (common), external connections 1 of 5; differentiator
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Two-level tenancy org -> workspaces with policy resolving org then workspace; operator lifecycle as a state machine on the tenant row (active, archived, deleting with fence generation, deleted) with transfer as an owner swap. Shared rooms: shared_room(host_org, room_id) plus org_link(host_org, guest_org, status); the host org's policy governs posting and apps, members authenticate in their own org, and the client shows an external marker and a consent pane on first contact. QM: a reconciler swaps the Slack adapter on config version change with rollback.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/settings/components/OrgDeletionDangerZone.tsx (org deletion exists, no archive or transfer)
verevonToday.gap: Single-level org tenant with deletion; no archive or ownership transfer, no parent org, no shared or cross-org rooms, no external chat connections (planned, blocked).

items.approach: Control Plane: org-core lifecycle (archived, transfer_pending) and owner-transfer flow first; defer a parent-org table until a customer needs it. After guests exist, org-to-org links and host-org-owned rooms with decisions that carry both orgs' policies, plus agent audience isolation as soon as any external participant can exist. External chat connections: wait for the Channel Plane; do not build adapters elsewhere.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane
items.risks: ZDR, residency and retention differ per org and one org's ZDR must hold for content its members post, which is hard to fit under per-org deny-by-default policies. Hierarchical policy resolution interacts with deny-by-default effect policies. The Channel Plane is docs-only, so this cannot be built as if it existed.

alreadyPlanned.where: External chat connections: apps/Channel Plane/docs/vision.md (docs-only); QM adoption plan S5.1 ADR adopted, S5.3 blocked

verevon.exactGap: org-core has single-level orgs with only active versus soft-deleted state (organizations.status default, deleted_at, RestoreOrganization) and no archive or owner-transfer, which the gateway and settings UI explicitly defer. A parent-like construct already exists in Control: auth-core org_group (host-org anchored) with per-org data_access and billing_consolidation grants, mirrored into billing-core billing_group_memberships and consumed by the account.data.read decision, but with no product UI. There are no cross-org Spaces or guests (registered Spaces are org-bound and presence treats cross-org rows as impossible), and external chat connections exist only as integration-corev2 data/inbox providers (Slack, Teams message read, Meta/WhatsApp), not as Space bridges.
reuse: auth-core org_group and org_group_grant (host-org account above orgs) instead of a new parent-org table
billing-core billing_group_memberships (plan inheritance mirror) and the account.data.read decision path
org-core deletion_ledger lifecycle (soft delete, restore, reminders) as the template for an archived and transfer_pending state machine
integration-corev2 Slack, Teams and Meta connections plus webhookorg resolver as the ingest side of external chat
user-core decision.go SignDecision for a decision that carries both orgs policy
verevon.constraints: Control is the only external-link authority and Application owns conversation mapping and delivery receipts per the adopted S5.1 surface-neutral ingress ADR (known only through the adoption plan; the ADR file lives outside the repo and was not read). Space membership is org-bound in Control, so cross-org rooms need a new Control membership and decision model (one org ZDR must hold for content its members post) and cannot be bolted onto Application projections. Space access never widens an owner-plane ACL, and an external audience must restrict agents to a context without org memory or keys. Channel Plane is docs-only and its vision covers customer-facing widget and commerce channels, not Slack or Teams workspace bridges.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Replace "defer a parent-org table" with "reuse the shipped org_group and add UI plus lifecycle". Drop the blanket claim that external chat workspace connections must wait for Channel Plane: Channel Plane vision targets widgets, Shopify, WooCommerce and WordPress, and S5.1 left open whether the adapter lives in Channel Plane or elsewhere while assigning identity links to Control and mapping/delivery to Application. The cheap slice (org archive plus owner transfer) is independent of guests and should be its own row.
verevon.effortNote: XL stands only for shared cross-org rooms. Org archive plus owner transfer is M (org-core state, auth-core owner-role swap, gateway contract, settings UI); an org_group admin UI is S to M.
verevon.verdictReason: Status partial is right, but the item misses the existing org_group parent construct and mislabels where external chat connections belong; it should be reworded and split into org lifecycle (M), org_group UI (S to M) and shared rooms (XL, post-guests).

items.title: Assurance long tail: hash-chained audit, formal decision model, supply-chain gates, EU-posture pinning, credential expiry states
items.summary: Five independent assurance items for regulated buyers, taken after the audit export exists. (1) Chain audit rows (entry_hash over seq, actor, action, metadata, prev_hash) with a signed daily head checkpoint and a verify endpoint. (2) Model Space decision issuance in TLA+ or PlusCal, checking 'Space access never widens an owner ACL' and 'no effect without a fresh decision'. (3) Add supply-chain gates: dependency cooldown, cargo-deny and govulncheck across all Rust and Go services, signed images. (4) State an EU-only posture and pin model-provider region per org. (5) Credential lifecycle states with expiry warnings in agent settings.
items.whyItMatters: None of these block the Space, but they answer the questions enterprise security questionnaires ask and make Verevon's signed-authority design verifiable. Each facet is small and independent.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: buzz
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: Hash chain and formal specs: 1 of 5 each (buzz); supply chain: 2 of 5 (buzz, qm); residency: 2 of 5 (slack, teams); credential lifecycle: 1 of 5 (grokbot).
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Audit: entry hash over the tenant id, sequence, time, event, actor, action, canonical metadata and previous hash, with an external signed anchor. Formal: spec the multi-party protocol, mutate the spec to prove the invariants are not vacuous, replay service traces against the model. Supply chain: 7-day package cooldown, prod dependency audit, signed images with digest pins. Residency: per-org home region in Control that routes data-plane calls. Credentials: state, expires_at and a warn or enforce mode with owner notice.

evidence: apps/Control Plane/audit-core/internal/store/schema.sql:11-33 (payload_hash per event, but no prev_hash or entry_hash chain; a grep found none)
A search to depth 4 of apps/ found no TLA+, Alloy or Tamarin files

.github/workflows/verevonv3-security.yml:26-51 (pnpm audit at high), quarry-v2-ci.yml:231-240 (cargo audit and govulncheck), secret-scan.yml and dependabot.yml; no release-age policy or image signing found by grep of workflows

apps/Control Plane/user-core/internal/spaces/authority.go:149-153 (a residency string is bound into every decision) and apps/Control Plane/org-core/internal/org/types.go:60-68 (dormant data_residency column); no routing or provider pinning seen
apps/Ingestion Plane/integration-corev2 credential model: expiry states not checked
verevonToday.gap: Some supply-chain checks exist for the frontend and Quarry only; the rest is absent or unchecked. Residency is a label with no enforcement.

items.approach: audit-core: add prev_hash and entry_hash with per-org serialised append and a signed checkpoint using existing key infrastructure. Repo CI: min-release-age, cargo-deny and govulncheck for every service, image signing in the deploy pipeline. Model Plane inference routing: per-org provider-region pinning plus a documented EU-only deployment statement (full multi-region stacks are out of scope). integration-corev2 and Frontend: credential state, expiry and warnings, aligned with the S3.4 credential broker. Formal model: write the decision protocol spec alongside the Space authority ADR.
items.planeOwner: Control Plane (audit-core) with Support Plane (CI), Model Plane (routing) and Ingestion Plane (credentials)
items.risks: Append serialisation limits audit throughput; checkpoint key management; formal models drift from code unless trace-checked; CI friction; sub-processor residency (Novu, Convex) limits what 'EU-only' can claim.

alreadyPlanned.where: Credential expiry and revocation are in apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/docs/VEREVON_QM_COMPARISON_AND_ADOPTION_PLAN_2026-08-13.md S3.4; the other facets are not planned.

verevon.exactGap: Per facet: audit-core keeps only a per-event sha256 payload_hash used for idempotent conflict detection (no prev_hash, entry_hash, checkpoint or verify route; only GET and POST /v1/audit), and no TLA+, Alloy or Tamarin artefacts exist under apps. Supply-chain gates are partial and uneven: blocking pnpm audit (high) and gitleaks for the frontend and repo, weekly Dependabot only for frontend npm, gateway cargo and actions, Quarry-only cargo audit plus a continue-on-error govulncheck, pnpm 11 with a minimumReleaseAgeExclude list (INF: a release-age gate is active though no value is set), and no cargo-deny, image signing or gates for Control, Model or Data services. Residency is a label (org-core data_residency column unused, Space EffectPolicy residency string bound into decisions, deploy-wide EU region allowlist and one AZURE region per process in inference-core, no per-org routing), and integration-corev2 already tracks connection status needs_refresh plus access_token_expires_at with reconnect warnings in Settings and Inbox, so only proactive expiry warnings and Space credential grants (S3.4, plan only) are missing.
reuse: audit-core payload_hash, source_stream_sequence and ON CONFLICT dedupe as the starting point for an entry hash
user-core decision.go Ed25519 SigningKey and VerifyDecision for signing daily audit head checkpoints
inference-core EU_AZURE_REGIONS, deny-by-default non-EU embedding gate and Space EffectPolicy.Residency as the residency foundation
org-core data_residency column (dormant) as the per-org pin source
integration-corev2 Connection status plus AccessTokenExpiresAt and the existing isFailedIntegrationStatus UI for credential expiry states
existing CI workflows verevonv3-security.yml, secret-scan.yml, quarry-v2-ci.yml and dependabot.yml as the ones to extend
verevon.constraints: audit-core is Control-owned and ingests at-least-once from NATS with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a hash chain needs per-org serialised append in insert order and will limit throughput; audit events must stay ids and hashes only (audit is not a shadow store, retention-schedule). Residency pinning is a Control policy that Model Plane enforces at routing time; Model must not read org-core tables, so the pin has to arrive through claims or a Control decision. Credential expiry belongs with the Control-owned credential grants planned in S3.4 (reuse resource grants, no new keychain). Sub-processor residency (Novu, Convex) limits any EU-only claim.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Treat as five independent rows rather than one L item: (1) audit hash chain, (2) formal decision model, (3) supply-chain gates, (4) per-org residency, (5) credential expiry. Start supply chain by tightening what exists (make Quarry govulncheck blocking, add cargo audit and govulncheck to Model, Control and Data CI, add an explicit minimumReleaseAge value and Dependabot cooldown) before adding cargo-deny and image signing. Fold credential expiry into S3.4 and state that reactive needs_refresh already ships. Make residency start from the org-core column and Space EffectPolicy residency and move inference-core from one region per process to a per-org selection.
verevon.effortNote: L holds only as an aggregate. Individually: hash chain M, formal spec M, supply-chain gates M, residency L (multi-region deployments are out of scope; routing only is M), credential warnings S.
verevon.verdictReason: Status partial is right, but three facets are further along than the item implies (supply-chain checks, residency label and gates, credential status) and the bundle hides five unrelated owners; split it and correct the facet statuses.

items.title: Long-tail Space UX, build on demand: multiview tiling, agent-led first-run welcome, What's New and admin notices, non-web link interstitial
items.summary: Four independent slices, none of which blocks the vision. (a) Multiview: tile several rooms or agent sessions with a dockview-style layout once AuxPane and run components are self-contained. (b) Welcome: seed the org room with an agent introduction and role/tools questions that feed the three agent templates. (c) What's New panel and admin-only notices for policy rollout. (d) Route non-http(s) links in agent-posted content through a confirmation with per-host memory.
items.whyItMatters: Multiview is a real edge for operators supervising several agents (QM only); a welcome post where an agent introduces itself removes the empty-room first impression; admin notices help owners learn which deny-by-default agent policies to enable; and a link gate reduces risk from model-generated links.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: QM (multiview with tile limits and per-pane density); Grok Bot (onboarding flow and fail-open gate); Teams (feedback, What's New, admin campaigns); Slack (protocol interstitial with per-host allowlist)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: multiview 1 of 5 (QM); onboarding 2 of 5 (Grok Bot, Buzz); What's New 1 of 5 (Teams); link interstitial 1 of 5 (Slack); differentiator to unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Multiview: dockview-core layout with MAX_TILES = 16, per-pane drag payloads and a serialised layout synced per user. Onboarding: gate state machine checking -> probe -> landed | onboarding | shell with a saved seen flag that fails open for returning users. What's New: feed items with an index and campaigns targeted by role and flag. Interstitial: intercept non-http(s) schemes, show a modal, store an allowlist of {protocol, hostname} per user.

evidence: apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/onboarding/components/steps/IntroStep.tsx and apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/src/features/spaces/components/SpacesIndexPage.tsx:36-47 (org onboarding and self-healing /spaces exist; no Space first run)
verevonToday.gap: Multiview absent; no Space-specific first run (welcome content, agent introduction, role/tools questions); a grep for whats-new/WhatsNew finds nothing, though "feedback" appears in 36 files of unknown purpose; how agent-posted non-web links are rendered (markdown link sanitiser in chat components) is not checked.

items.approach: Frontend Plane for all four. Multiview after AuxPane (F-t1-001 (R-t1-12-01)), push realtime (a 6 s poll per tile multiplies polling cost) and self-contained room and run components. Welcome: seed a post and template agent proposals that a human confirms (agents may not create bindings themselves), with claims derived from observed facts, not timers. What's New from a static release feed, admin notices through Control role targeting. Link gate: extend the markdown link sanitiser so non-http(s) schemes never auto-open.
dependencies: AuxPane shell (F-t1-001 (R-t1-12-01)) and push realtime (category 09) for multiview
Human-only post path (category 01) and existing agent templates for the welcome
items.planeOwner: Frontend Plane
items.risks: Tile polling cost; agents must not self-create bindings; notice noise. Verify the link-rendering and feedback surfaces before scoping slices (c) and (d).

verevon.exactGap: None of the four slices exists: SpacePage mounts one room per route (App.tsx:182) and AgentRunConsole is a prop-less page route with local state rather than a tile (AgentRunConsole.tsx:168); the only first-run content is the static SpaceRoomIntro (SpaceRoomTimeline.tsx:433), shown when a room has no posts, plus three static name-and-instructions templates (SpaceCreateAgentDialog.tsx:43), and there is no What's New or admin-notice surface (notification-core only carries per-user events). The link slice is really a missing safeguard: the markdown renderer that Space uses for agent posts emits an anchor from any [text](url) target with no scheme allowlist (chat-media-markdown.tsx:1279), so mailto:, tel: and custom app schemes pass, and only the production nginx CSP without script-src 'unsafe-inline' should keep javascript: links inert (INF, not tested).
reuse: SpaceRoomIntro plus the three AGENT_TEMPLATES for a human-confirmed welcome
ensure_organization_room action and the SpacesIndexPage org-room self-heal as the first-run hook
notification-core and gateway notifications.rs for admin notices (needs a new org-targeted event)
streamRunEvents and the run-event rendering in AgentRunConsole.tsx once extracted into a props-driven component
parseInline in chat-media-markdown.tsx as the single place for a link scheme allowlist
verevon.constraints: Frontend Plane owns all four slices, but admin notices need an Application Plane (notification-core) org-targeted event plus Control role targeting, and the welcome must stay human-confirmed because agents may not create bindings and Space authority is Control-owned. Multiview multiplies the 6 s room poll (SpacePage.tsx:87) and each tile must keep its own Control context recheck. Link handling must keep rendering untrusted model output as data and never auto-open.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Split the item: pull the link slice out of build-on-demand and ship a scheme allowlist (http, https, mailto) in parseInline now, covering both the [text](url) and bare-URL branches and rendering other schemes as plain text; add the per-host interstitial only if non-web schemes are later wanted. Build the welcome as an extension of SpaceRoomIntro and the existing templates rather than a seeded agent post. Keep multiview behind a run-event component extracted from AgentRunConsole and behind push realtime.
verevon.effortNote: Unchanged for the bundle, but the slices are uneven: link scheme allowlist S, welcome M, What's New and admin notices M (new org broadcast event), multiview L.
verevon.verdictReason: Nothing proposed exists, so it stays build-on-demand, but the link slice is a missing safeguard rather than polish and AgentRunConsole is not a reusable tile today, so the item should say both.

items.title: Reverse channel so a user's own computer can run agent tool requests without inbound ports (later; cloud browser first)
items.summary: If the "agent has its own PC" vision extends to the user's machine, add a local executor daemon that keeps an outbound SSE open through the gateway, receives Model-proposed tool requests, checks them against a local policy, executes, and posts results back with the request id, with heartbeat, a polling fallback and supervised restart. Do this only after the cloud sandbox and browser path is solid, and keep the rule that the Model proposes and the executor decides.
items.whyItMatters: It is the one reference capability that makes an agent act on the real desktop and the most distinctive part of the Grok Bot half of the vision, but it adds a large local-execution attack surface and only Grok Bot ships it. The gateway already streams live browser frames and supports human takeover for cloud browser runs, which covers most needs first.

referenceBestPractice.bestSource: Grok Bot (daemon opens GET /local-exec/requests as SSE, POSTs results back; one daemon serves several accounts; discovery record with pid and generation; respawn limits)
referenceBestPractice.prevalence: 1 of 5; unique
referenceBestPractice.mechanism: Daemon keeps an outbound SSE with heartbeat; on a request frame it executes under local policy and POSTs the result with the request id; if the stream fails it polls a pending endpoint; the app adopts or replaces the daemon via a discovery record.

verevonToday.gap: No local agent or daemon was found by the comparator (not exhaustively searched). SRC: for cloud browsers the gateway exposes live-frame streams, human_takeover and agent_control capabilities; the space baselines list an agent PC or browser inside the room as absent and only RustDesk remote-support configuration exists.

items.approach: Ingestion Plane executor (Quarry-style) that only executes Model-proposed actions after a local policy check, with an outbound SSE through the gateway and a request/response contract using Control-signed grants and receipts; reuse the browser live-frame channel for viewing. Decide first whether a Space agent should ever reach a user machine, then design the policy model.
items.planeOwner: Ingestion Plane
items.risks: Large security surface (local code execution and credential exposure); must preserve the Model-proposes, executor-decides split and ZDR for anything captured locally.

verevon.exactGap: No agent tool-request executor on a user machine exists: nothing opens an outbound SSE or polling channel to receive Model-proposed tool requests, and there is no Control-signed grant or receipt protocol for local execution. A native installable host agent already exists, though (apps/Endpoint Plane, Verevon Agent, Rust): it registers outbound with hbbs/hbbr, captures the screen, injects input and gates control with a native consent prompt, but as a RustDesk-compatible remote-desktop host for human support, with identity only a local file and a Control device-identity contract explicitly deferred. The cloud-first path the item asks for is largely there: gateway browser routes give live frames, agent_control/human_takeover and persistent profiles, and sandbox-manager has leases, a durable workspace manifest, snapshots and a process registry.
evidence: apps/Endpoint Plane/docs/architecture.md:1-20 (native Verevon Agent, host side of the RustDesk protocol)
apps/Endpoint Plane/docs/architecture.md:305-318 (Control-Plane identity contract for the agent, file transfer, installer out of scope)
apps/Endpoint Plane/docs/architecture.md:480-500 (consent policy hardcoded; no mid-session revoke; audio and file transfer unbuilt)
apps/Endpoint Plane/src/main.rs:1-50 (registers with hbbs, single session, local identity file, input gated by consent)
apps/Endpoint Plane/src/consent.rs:1-40 (native Yes/No prompt; permanent-password sessions skip it)
apps/Support Plane/README.md:55-70 (Support Plane knows nothing about Verevon sessions or users; backend token mapping is product logic)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/remote_support.rs:1-40 (config only; the session never transits the gateway)
apps/Frontend Plane/verevonv3/apps/gateway/src/domains/browser.rs:2540-2578 (Quarry owner projection; capability list incl. human_takeover, agent_control, persistent_profile)
apps/Model Plane/rust/services/execution-core/src/sandbox.rs:265-300 (local executor profile: credential-free, one child process, no durable workspace)
apps/Model Plane/go/services/sandbox-manager/internal/workspace/store.go:1-40 (durable layered workspace manifest) and internal/{lease,snapshot,process} directories listed
apps/Model Plane/go/services/capability-core/internal/roadmap/data.go:55-80 (says sandbox-manager and browser-broker are not implemented: stale, sandbox-manager has real internals)
CLAUDE.md:22-37 (Model proposes, Quarry executes; Support Plane owns no session state; Endpoint Plane not listed)
reuse: apps/Endpoint Plane Verevon Agent (outbound registration in va-net, consent.rs, va-capture, va-input) as the daemon to extend
Support Plane hbbs/hbbr rendezvous for device presence
gateway browser live-frame channel and AgentControl/HumanTakeover control modes for viewing and takeover
Control-signed decision and receipt patterns (Space capability decision, mail-task-v1) for local-execution grants
sandbox-manager lease/workspace/process registry as the cloud computer the item says must come first
verevon.constraints: Model proposes, an executor decides and executes: for a user machine the executor would be the Endpoint agent, a new executor class beyond Quarry (browser) and Model Plane sandboxes (tools). Endpoint Plane is absent from CLAUDE.md's plane list, and grep finds no mention of it in master-ownership-matrix.md or CODEBASE_INFORMATION_SYSTEM.md, so ownership must be registered before building on it. Support Plane owns no user, session or billing state and its sessions bypass the gateway, so an SSE reverse channel through the gateway is a new traffic class. ZDR must propagate to anything captured locally and returned to the Model, and a user machine is personal-resource authority that Space membership must never widen (Control grants per user, never shared into a room by default). The agent's permanent-password unattended mode must not become agent authority.
verevon.approachAdjustment: Do not add an Ingestion Plane Quarry-style executor for this. Register Endpoint Plane ownership, then extend the Verevon Agent with a second policy-gated channel for agent tool requests (outbound stream plus polling fallback), driven by Control-signed grants and receipts, with a per-capability local policy (start observation-only). Keep the cloud sandbox and browser first, as the item says, and decide first whether a Space agent should ever reach a user machine. The item's 'no local agent was found' premise is wrong and should be removed.
verevon.effortNote: Slightly lower than a from-scratch daemon because the native shell, outbound registration and consent prompt exist, but a Control device-identity contract, grant/receipt protocol, local policy engine and cross-platform packaging are all new and the agent is Windows-only today.
verevon.verdictReason: The capability is still absent, but the item misdescribes the baseline (a native host agent exists) and mis-places the executor in the Ingestion Plane; keep it as a late nice-to-have with the corrected foundation.
